name: Vanilla Factions Expanded - Pirates
author: Oskar Potocki, Sarg Bjornson, erdelf, Roolo, Smash Phil, Taranchuk, xrushha, Kikohi, legodude17
description:
One faction that always felt a little bit 'un-expanded' in vanilla RimWorld is the pirate faction. They feel more like evil outlanders than anything unique, and they don't really threaten late game colonies, nor do they provide engaging content in any way, shape or form. It always annoyed me that they are industrial tier only and don't even spawn with charge rifles anymore.
  
  Roolo, Smash Phil and I are launching a new pirate survival video game inspired by RimWorld on Kickstarter. It's called Cursed Crew if anyone would like to check it out. I figured that the best way to promote the game through the channels I know a lot about is to create a mod, ideally a factions expanded mod, expanding pirates. Of course there is no boats and sea-faring pirates in RimWorld, but there are space pirates, so let's expand them!
  
  Vanilla Factions Expanded - Pirates greatly expands the vanilla pirate faction by adding new events, technology, defense means etc. We are also adding two new factions - Junkers, which are inspired by the hordes of Huns, but instead of riding horses, they weld themselves inside powerful warcaskets; and Mercenaries, a spacer-tech faction of 'legal', sanctioned pirates that you can befriend!
  
  You can now use your Comms console to hire pirates too! Pirates you hire join you for a period of time, but they come with a hefty price.
  
  And most importantly, you can now create warcaskets - steel suits of industrial-tier armor, a powered-armor precursor, around your pawns. Fully customizable, with unique weapons and armor graphics!
  
  And with Ideology, you can enjoy a new Pirate meme, with singing sea shanties and much more important camaraderie!
  
  Do check out Cursed Crew, as if you liked RimWorld, I'm sure you will like our take on rogue-like survival, sailing the endless ocean and fighting dangerous, mythical creatures.

name: Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Memes and Structures
author: Oskar Potocki, Sarg Bjornson, Chowder
description:
Vanilla Ideology Expanded is a mini-series of mods aimed at expanding the content in ideology - be it memes, relics and symbols or icons alike.
	
The goal of the Memes and Structures mod is to add unique memes, and… well, structures to your game. For some reason certain obvious choices like Shinto, Taoism and Eldritch were missing from the base DLC, and this mod is here to introduce them to the ideology creation.
With unique memes, players will be able to diversify their playthrough every time they play. This should increase longevity of the game and also make it way more unique and personalised.

This mod adds 36 new memes, alongside many new structures, rituals, precepts, specialist roles, items, objects and mechanics. It should greatly expand what Ideology has to offer, and meshes nicely with the rest of the DLC. With Vanilla Ideology Expanded - Memes and Structures you will be able to create powerful psykers that simply love chocolate, a corporate scrap trading business, a fishing republic, a bunch of god-king radicals, mechanoid technocratic union and much, much more.

name: Pick Up And Haul - Shared Storage Access
description:
Do your pawns queue outside a huge single-tile storage building while only one of them actually carries anything in? Ever seen "no storage space" when the building is nowhere near full?

The reason is simple: one hauler can reserve the entire destination tile. This is barely noticeable with stockpile zones, but a Stone Cellar or another deep-storage building may hold dozens or hundreds of stacks in one tile. While the first colonist, mech, or animal is delivering an item, everyone else treats the whole storage building as occupied.

This patch allows several haulers to share the same multi-stack storage tile at once. The limit scales with its capacity: a 3-stack container allows up to 3 haulers, while larger storage allows more, up to a hard limit of 32. Ordinary shelves, stockpile cells, graves, storage priorities, routes, and item filters are not changed.

The patch also helps Pick Up And Haul build mixed trips for these buildings, allowing accepted items such as wood, steel, and meat to be carried together instead of restricting a trip to one item type.

OPTIONAL: Enable "Allow shared source stack reservations" in mod settings to let up to 10 haulers reserve separate quantities from the same oversized source stack. This is useful with OgreStack and similar mods. The option affects only storage-hauling jobs; ordinary stacks that one pawn can take completely remain exclusive. The feature is experimental and disabled by default.

OPTIONAL VEHICLE FRAMEWORK SUPPORT: Enable "Allow shared vehicle cargo loading" to let cargo loaders reserve separate quantities from the same item stack. This is a separate experimental option, disabled by default, and can be used alone or together with shared source stacks. It supports loading selected cargo into vehicles on the map; caravan gathering, passengers, refuelling and turret ammunition are excluded. Vehicle Framework is optional.

EXAMPLE: The Stone Cellar from Adaptive Primitive Storage occupies one tile but stores up to 175 stacks. With this patch, several haulers may deliver to it at the same time instead of the first one blocking the cellar for everyone else.

WHO NEEDS THIS: players using Pick Up And Haul together with single-tile storage buildings that hold multiple item stacks.

Requires Harmony and Pick Up And Haul. Tested with Adaptive Storage Framework and Adaptive Primitive Storage.

NOT NEEDED WITH HAULER'S DREAM: that mod is a complete hauling overhaul which replaces Pick Up And Haul, and it already provides shared storage access as part of its own routing. This patch is for players who want to keep using Pick Up And Haul itself.

Unofficial compatibility patch. Safe to add to or remove from an existing save between game launches.

name: Rimesis
author: Font
description:
Rimesis turns a small number of otherwise anonymous enemy raiders into persistent recurring antagonists with a personal history against the colony.

They remember killers, weapons, wounds, destroyed body parts, escape, extraction, captivity, betrayal, successful raids, and settlements lost to the player. When they return, they remain the same character - but their skills, equipment, armor, implants, companions, and tactics grow with their history.

Destroying a faction's final settlement triggers a configurable series of escalating retaliation raids from that exact faction, even after RimWorld marks it defeated. Campaign waves wait for earlier attackers to leave the field so the pressure remains severe without becoming an unavoidable pileup.

Each Rimesis receives a recognizable combat focus and tactical style. They may command sieges, breaches, flanking groups, elite troops, hordes, mechs, trained animals, vehicles, or Warcasket equipment when supported content is active. Their complete story remains available in the Chronicle, including after permanent death.

No DLC is required. Royalty, Biotech, Anomaly, Odyssey, RimHUD, Trauma and Integrity, Fantasy Biotech, Giddy-Up 2, Mount Passengers, Vehicle Raid Framework, Exosuit Framework, VFE Pirates, Isekai RPG Leveling, Eternal Pawns, and compatible modded equipment activate additional features only when available.

name: Vanilla Genetics Expanded
author: Sarg, erdelf, Oskar Potocki, Luizi, Reann Shepard
description:
Vanilla Genetics Expanded is an overhaul to a popular mod by Sarg Bjornson called Genetic Rim. The mechanics of the predecessor have been improved greatly to fit Vanilla Expanded playstyle, offering many new paths to explore in a mid to late game colony. You can now incubate unique hybrids using brand new genetic engineering system, utilising powerful boosters and genoframes to create animals stronger, smarter and quicker than anything you've ever seen. Stay vigilant though, as there is always a chance of an experiment failing, producing one of many new failure outcomes - such as cute and cuddly fleshlings, or powerful, ever-expanding fleshgrowth.

name: Achtung!
author: Andreas Pardeike
description:
Command your colonists like a boss!

The Achtung! mod enhances how you control RimWorld. You will get more control on how to position your colonists and how they take job orders.

In a nutshell you can:

- position your drafted colonists along a line
- move them in formation
- give orders to multiple colonists at once
- force jobs so they get uninterrupted attention
- haul and repair outside allowed areas


EXAMPLES

(*) Save time by issuing a command with more than one colonist selected. For example: select three brawlers and right click an enemy, then choose "melee". Done.

(*) In combat, position colonists equally spaced in door openings. Select multiple drafted colonists and with the right mouse button drag a line. Achtung! will move your colonists to equally spaced positions in real time. 10 colonists into 10 doors? No problem!

(*) Fall back a few steps with a group of colonists? Easy. Select them and hold the configured key to move them relative to their current formation. You can even rotate the formation with the standard rotation keys.

(*) Make sure that wall and the sandbags are build before the raid arrives. No cloudwatching or eating allowed! Use the [Force] button that Achtung! adds to all "Prioritize..." menus and you can be sure that all assigned work will be done.

(*) Want one colonist harvest and another sow these three fields? Force them to their tasks and queue up non-adjacted fields by simply adding forced work on them (like ordinary jobs but without the shift key).

(*) Treat all injured colonists in their beds? Select a doctor, choose "Prioritize tending... [Force]" and increase the search range so nearby patients will be included (you will see a small "!" on all forced job). Then focus on other important stuff because you can be sure it's done.

The original three Achtung! commands "Clean Room", "Fight Fire" or "Sow Zone/Room" still exist because they do stuff a bit smarter than the build in prioritized work commands.


SETTINGS

Achtung uses the default way to access mod settings. There, you find switches to turn certain features on/off and you can change the default keys to your liking.


ADDING AND REMOVING:

Achtung can be added to any existing game. It usually does not modify save state for saved games to avoid a dependency on it. However, a side effect of the provided custom jobs is that when save the game and your colonists are actively running an Achtung job this will be saved too thus creating a dependency to Achtung. Workaround: open the saved game with Achtung, cancel all Achtung jobs and save it again. This will "clean" the save and remove the dependency.


FEEDBACK

Please send me feedback and rate and recommend my mod whenever possible. The three main places to do so are

Ludeon Forums: https://ludeon.com/forums/index.php?topic=22130.0

Steam Workshop:
http://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/comments/730936602

GitHub:
https://github.com/pardeike/Achtung2/releases/latest

Free. As in free beer. Copy, learn and be respectful.

name: Desert Vehicle Reskin — Alpha Vehicles Neolithic
author: Mandrake
description:
Redraws the draught animals in Alpha Vehicles - Neolithic so its carts read as desert, not as medieval Europe.

Mostly texture overrides: every art file here sits at the exact path the donor's own ThingDef already asks for, so the vehicles, their stats and their research stay entirely the donor's, and Alpha Vehicles - Neolithic itself is never edited.

Two things go beyond art. A pair of XML PatchOperations retint and rename the dog sled as an eopie sled, and a small Harmony assembly widens what the draught vehicles will burn: the donor gives each cart exactly one fuel ThingDef (Hay for the chariots, ox cart and covered carriage; Kibble for the sled) because its fuel comp holds a single ThingDef and no ThingFilter, so there is no XML route to widen it. The patch makes any nutrition-giving vegetable-type food count — anything whose foodType carries Plant, VegetableOrFruit or Meal, excluding meat, animal products and drugs — plus, always, whatever the vehicle already declared, so nothing that fuels a cart today stops fuelling it. No defName is listed anywhere, so modded crops qualify on their own.

WHY THE ANIMAL AND NOT THE CART

The draught animals are drawn INTO the vehicle texture rather than spawned as pawns, so replacing them is a per-file art edit. The carts themselves are fine: an ox cart, a covered carriage and a chariot are as at home on a desert world as anywhere. Only what pulls them is off-theme.

Seven of the donor's vehicles are untouched because they have no animal to replace — the wheelbarrow, hwacha, rickshaw and palanquin are human-powered, the balloon is Air, and the row boat and outrigger canoe are Sea.

CONTENTS

  Things/Vehicles/Land/Tier0/DogSled/AV_DogSled_{north,south,east}
      A team of two eopies in place of four dogs. The eopie is Tatooine's
      canonical beast of burden; four dogs at a sled's scale read as a polar
      expedition. Two animals rather than four because the eopie is the larger
      beast — the harness traces are re-routed as a two-animal Y.
      Each facing is drawn, not mirrored: south is a head-on pair abreast,
      north is a rear view with no snout and the rigging hanging down, east is
      a side profile with the pair stacked vertically and the rigging to the
      left.

  Things/Vehicles/Land/Tier0/DogSled/AV_DogSled_{north,south,east}m
      The paired colour masks, edited in step with the art. Vehicle Framework
      reads these for its colour and pattern system, so a mask left stale
      makes the new animal refuse to tint. Note the donor's suffix convention:
      the "m" is appended to the facing (AV_DogSled_southm), not separated
      (AV_DogSled_south_m).

LOAD ORDER MATTERS HERE

Alpha Vehicles - Neolithic ships its vehicle art as loose PNGs, not as an AssetBundle. Between two loose files at the same path RimWorld resolves by load order, so this mod must load AFTER the donor or the donor's own art wins and nothing here is visible. That is the opposite of an AssetBundle override, where a loose file wins regardless of order.

name: Jawa Doctrine Patches

description:

name: RimMandrake - Star Wars Races
author: mandrake
description:
69 Star Wars species, owned outright, so the three colliding xenotype mods can be switched off.

Star Wars Xenotypes, Outer Rim - Galactic Diversity and [BTD] Xenotype REMIX each ship an overlapping set of the same species. They collide, and BTD carries a Harmony assembly whose only job is to delete the duplicates and keep its own. This mod ends that by owning the composition: the species, their genes, their head types and their art live here, and none of the three donors needs to be installed.

CREDIT. The art and the gene design are not ours.
- Star Wars Xenotypes, by guy762 - Workshop 2915192253. 112 genes and their textures are copied from it.
- Outer Rim - Galactic Diversity, by Neronix17 - Workshop 2980427615. 22 genes, the head types and the species icons are copied from it. Its 1.6 release routes loading at a folder that no longer holds its loose art; the sprites here are recovered from the folder it left behind, which is why they render again.
- [BTD] Xenotype REMIX, by beeteedubs - Workshop 3458153185. The species reconciliation is its work. Its hand-curated equivalence table is what decides which donor supplies each species, and the gene lists are inherited from it.

Species NAMES come with them. 48 name-generating rule packs and the word lists they read are copied too - a rule pack without its Languages/English/Strings word lists resolves and produces nothing - so a Twi'lek is still named like a Twi'lek with every donor off. Four namers that Star Wars Xenotypes had commented out are wired back up here; they were disabled to avoid overriding forced names on another mod's hero pawnkinds, which reference that mod's xenotypes and not ours.

Outer Rim's sixteen species pawn kinds are copied as well, with both of their abstract parents, because a faction that fields them directly loses those raids and caravans outright when that mod leaves.

The RSW_MandrakeJawa xenotype and its four genes - skittish, hooded face, and the orange and amber big-eye colours with their glow sprite - are authored here rather than copied, and live in this mod because the Jawa are a species like any other.

Nothing generic was copied. Genes that belong to Biotech, Core, Outland Genetics, Integrated Genes, LFS Genes Expanded - Eyes and Big and Small remain theirs; those mods are dependencies and must stay installed.

name: Jawa Armoury Rebalance
author: Mandrake
description:
Restretches the weapon ladder so the armoury matches the setting's
physical laws instead of RimWorld's defaults.

The problem it fixes, measured on this exact mod set: the median ranged weapon
did 12 damage and the median BLASTER did 10 — against a human fist at 8.2. Four
in five weapons needed three or more hits to drop an unarmoured person, a wooden
club outperformed a blaster rifle, and a turbolaser did 80, only 1.45x a vanilla
sniper turret. Everything from fist to capital battery lived inside a 10x range.

What changes:
  standard blaster    -> 24-34    1-2 shots unarmoured, ~5 vs advanced armour
  heavy blaster       -> 52-72    deliberately breaks the 5-shot contract
  slugthrower         -> 18-36    spread wide; the answer to desert megafauna
  vibro               -> 35-52    the anti-ablative counter
  lightsaber          -> 80-120   supreme vs flesh (and useless vs vehicle plate)
  turbolaser          -> 800-2000 two orders above personal weapons

What deliberately does NOT change: ion, stun, EMP, sonic and disruptor weapons
keep their near-zero damage. The verb IS the weapon — an ion gun that kills is
just a worse blaster. Explosives are untouched too: blast has no hard counter,
so it is balanced by scarcity alone.

Relative ordering inside every weapon family is preserved — this restretches the
ladder, it does not flatten it.

Rationale: worldbuilding/setting_physics.md (the 18 laws) and
worldbuilding/balance_paradigm.md (why we change any value at all).

name: RimMandrake: SW — Gizka Stowaway
author: mandrake
description:
GIZKA_TRIBBLE_ADAPTATION_1 — the KotOR ship-pest, built as a found-aboard EVENT, never a storyteller threat roll.

The creature itself is NOT ours: `Gizka` (ThingDef/PawnKindDef/BodyDef, art, sounds, name generators, egg items) ships in Star Wars Animal Collection (Continued), `mlie.starwarsanimalcollection`. This mod adds only what that mod does not have: the discovery event, the escalation, the exits and their prices.

Discovery rides four things the PLAYER did, each individually toggleable: a gravship landing (Harmony postfix on `RimWorld.Scenario.PostGravshipLanded` — the confirmed hook, GIZKA_HOLD_HOOK_SPIKE_1), deconstructing wreck/ship-chunk salvage, a completed trade, and a quest ending in success (the "free gift" gag). Exactly one gizka arrives, tame, with a warm letter.

It then breeds. Only event-lineage gizka carry `RSW_GizkaFecundity`, a per-pawn hediff whose comp replicates asexually while the animal is FED and WARM — comfort is the fuse, and cold or hunger stalls it. Offspring inherit the hediff. Four stages (Cute / Underfoot / Infestation / Plague), each announcing itself in a letter BEFORE its cost lands, and the Infestation stage starts gizka-chewed breakdowns on powered buildings that share a room with them.

Five priced exits, all riding vanilla: cull (vanilla slaughter/bond mood plus `RSW_GizkaWatchedCull`), sell onward (the Jawa scam — the donor's MarketValue 100 is patched to 15 so the scam stays funny and never becomes income), poison bait (`RSW_GizkaBait`, a craftable the animals eat), cold (vent the room below the breeding gate), or lean in and farm them (deliberately mediocre).

The anti-exponential law: the exponential belongs to the pest. Replication is capped and the interval stretches as the cap nears; every player income line is flat and linear.

Separately, on the owner's 2026-09-17 ruling, this mod patches the DONOR gizka's own reproduction numbers so the creature breeds crazily everywhere in the world — wild, bought or traded, not just event lineage. See Patches/RSW_GizkaDonorPatches.xml.

Every feature is gated in Mod Settings (MOD_OPTIONS_RETROFIT_1); all-off leaves the donor creature as ordinary fauna and this mod inert. Nothing here touches worldgen.

kind, invented and franchise-free per Q11a), and the owner ruled the same

patched onto the third-party donor. `SHOKK_SKIN_SHRINK_1` carried that out —

`RM_Webwork_SunScald`/`RM_CompEmergentSpawnOnDestroy` all now live in
`mandrake.rm.webwork`, and `RSW_Shokk_Wyyyschokk.xml` (the patch onto the
donor) is retired — the donor's own `Wyyyschokk` no longer gets any of this
mod's mechanics.

**What ships here now, and only this:**

  `RSW_Shokk_OllathrixSkin.xml` (`OLLATHRIX_OWNER_SPECIES_1`, S6 ruling 6 —
  "the skin patch lives RSW, tier-correct for a Star Wars creature's LOOK,
  usable by any Star Wars scenario"). Overlays the canon Wyyyschokk identity
  (label, labelPlural, description, all three lifeStages' bodyGraphicData
  texPath) onto `RM_Ollathrix`'s SAME defName when this mod is loaded — one
  def, two skins, never a second race. It never touches mechanics.

  `RSW_Shokk_FeraliskBrood.xml` (a DIFFERENT item, `FEVERWOOD_TWO_FRONT_LURE_1`
  — see that file's own header) — a hidden FactionDef the Fever Wood's
  `RM_MapComponent_TwoFrontLure` looks up by defName for its second raid
  front. It lives in this mod, not `RM_FeverWood`, because it references the
  donor `Wyyyschokk` PawnKindDef directly (genuine Star Wars IP, routed
  through this RSW-tier mod per Q11a) — unrelated to the skin/mechanism split

`RM_Ollathrix` is THE wyyyschokk (owner ruling 2026-10-03, `WYYYSCHOKK_IDENTITY_COLLISION_1`); no second
wyyyschokk def exists, and the TrophyCraft fang drop follows the Ollathrix.

Live proof is OWED beyond this mod's own prior quicktest verification of the
mechanisms this description now says moved out — nothing left here to
verify beyond the skin patch's static xpath match.

name: RimMandrake: Luminous Pigment
author: mandrake
description:
DEEPFIRE_PIGMENT_MOD_1 (design/RimMandrake/deepfire_luminous_pigment_spec.md, fully
ruled 2026-09-25/26). RimMandrake tier — every name here is invented, nothing is Star Wars IP

dye it makes whatever colour the dye gives glow. It comes from crowncarpet, a rainbow bacterial
mat found rarely on any ocean shore.

low commonality), the one-day fresh-mat clock (dies fast, dies at once if chilled —
CompMatVitality), the Deepfire press (a screw press and an alchemical retort welded together,
powered only, gated by a research project hidden until a mat is first seen), the refining recipe,

name: Jawa Ion Weapons (local)
author: mandrake
description:
Self-contained, industrial-tier Jawa ion armament for this run.

A single signature weapon — the Jawa Ion Blaster — plus its own ion damage type and a custom "ion buildup" stun hediff. Design goals:
- CAPTURE-NOT-KILL: the weapon disables, it does not draw blood. No lethal damage.
- TIERED BY TARGET: relies on the vanilla stun-resistance gradient — mechanoids/droids are overloaded almost instantly; flesh pawns resist and must be worn down by accumulated ion buildup before they collapse (alive) and can be arrested.
- NOT VERY DANGEROUS, REWARDS CUNNING + TERRAIN: low damage, slow warmup, long cooldown, modest range, accuracy falloff — you win by ganging up, using cover and chokes, and stacking stuns, not by out-shooting anyone.
- MOSTLY-XML, PLUS ONE SMALL ASSEMBLY: the ion mechanics are our own vanilla-EMP-based defs, but Assemblies/JawaIonWeapons.dll ships a single DamageWorker subclass, RimMandrake.StarWars.JawaIonWeapons.DamageWorker_IonBuildup, wired in as the workerClass of RSW_JawaIon_Damage. It exists so each hit deposits RSW_JawaIon_Stun severity, which vanilla's additionalHediffs cannot do for a non-injury damage type. It is load-bearing: if it fails to load, RSW_JawaIon_Damage cannot resolve its workerClass. It contains no Log calls, so it is SILENT whether it works or not — a clean log is not evidence about it either way. Verify from the def dump instead: RSW_JawaIon_Damage.workerClass must read "RimMandrake.StarWars.JawaIonWeapons.DamageWorker_IonBuildup".

The weapon's own gun art is bundled here (Textures/JawaIon/Weapon_JawaIonBlaster.png). For the fired look and sound it reuses Outer Rim - Core's ion bolt sprite and blaster audio, so Core is a required dependency (Core in turn pulls Vanilla Expanded Framework and Tabula Rasa).

The RSW_JawaIon_Stun hediff doubles as the "stun -> down" mechanic the capture pipeline (CPERS: Arrest Here) needs.

VEHICLE_ION_TIER_1 (2026-08-29): a second assembly, Assemblies/JawaIonVehicleTier.dll, gives the weapon a real effect against Vehicle Framework vehicles — droid-tier EMP amount, scaled LINEARLY by the vehicle's footprint area (an estimate of its volume relative to a droid's own 1x1) rather than the flesh tier's body-size-squared curve. Soft dependency: it self-disables with a log warning if Vehicle Framework is not loaded, same as the base weapon works without it.

name: RimStarWars — Bacta
author: mandrake
description:
BACTA_TANK_CORE_1 — the bacta tank and the fluid that fills it.

Bacta is not regeneration. It is healing, turned up: a pawn suspended in a powered, filled tank closes wounds and burns far faster than a hospital bed, and — given long enough — old scars and permanent physical injuries fade out entirely. Damaged organs mend. What bacta will NOT do is grow anything back: a missing kidney stays missing, a lost leg stays lost. It will not touch the brain, and it will not repair a mind.

Infections are helped only where medicine could have helped them. An untendable disease runs its course in the tank exactly as it would in a bed.

The point is the shape of a lost battle. Without bacta, a bad raid costs colonists. With it, a bad raid costs recovery time — pawns are out of the game while they float, and they come back.

Bacta itself cannot be made. It is bought from exotic and outlander traders, or taken off someone who had some. The tank drinks it while it works, and stops when the tank runs dry.

Off by default, in Mod Settings: revival of the recently dead. A fresh corpse of ours, retrieved within a tunable window of a few hours, can be carried into an empty tank and revived — minus whatever bacta can't fix. No missing part regrows, and the brain and mind are untouched either way.

No Harmony patches: the tank is a Building_Enterable with our own ThingComps, so nothing in the base game is rewritten.

name: Jawa Pawn Flavor — faction backstories and traits
author: Mandrake
description:
Faction-keyed backstories, childhoods and traits for the Ash'karr campaign — every faction answers "why raid them, why enslave theirs, why free them" differently.

Seventy-seven BackstoryDefs (30 childhoods, 47 adulthoods) across thirteen faction categories, thirteen TraitDefs, and a patch file wiring a backstory category filter into each faction.

DESIGN SOURCE: design/Jawa/pawn_flavor_design.md (the nine faction sets, rounds 1-4, owner-directed). The two Free Droid Enclave groupings carry their own reframed sets (Assembly = childhood, Service = adulthood).

WIRING MECHANISM (verified against 1.6 source, PawnBioAndNameGenerator.cs): a faction's backstoryFilters and its pawnkinds' filters merge at generation; each filter is picked by commonality, then a backstory from its categories. Our patch adds one filter per faction naming category JawaBSC_<Faction>. name: Wrecked Machines
author: Mandrake
description:
Ancient wreckage.

Ancient machines do not fail politely. They are found where they died — split open, scavenged, corroded, half-buried in their own slag — and some of them are still, faintly, working. Ancient technology is robust: it does not stop, it sags. A wrecked power cell still trickles current. Bring one home, study it, and build it back up one grade at a time.

Every treated machine sits on one ladder of grades:

  WRECKED      Dead, or nearly. Inert — except that a wrecked power source
               still trickles a faint current.
  KLUDGED      Works, badly, visibly bodged. About a fifth of the original.
  REFURBISHED  The ceiling you normally reach: three-quarters of the original,
               and still visibly a kludge. Needs scarce ancient components.
  ORIGINAL     The machine as it was built. Off by default — a Mod Setting
               allows full restoration.

Each grade is built over the one below it. Studying the wreck itself is how you
learn to restore it (with Research Reinvented, the wreck is the research
subject). Mobile machines are on the ladder too: salvaged power cells and
psychic emanators can be carried off and installed wherever they are needed.

Advancing a grade costs materials, tools and earned knowledge, never a research
grind alone. Every ratio is tunable in Mod Settings.

This mod ships its own art for all three states and does not replace or alter
any other mod's buildings. The donor mod's original Automated Smelter ThingDef
is left completely untouched — its stats, comps and recipes are unchanged, and
our smelter grades still run its own processes — but it no longer
appears in the Architect build menu, so a player cannot build a fresh one
alongside our grades. Vanilla's own hand-run electric smelter is untouched
and unrelated.

name: RimMandrake: FlowWorks
author: Mandrake
description:
Dig a channel, let a fluid flow into it: a species- and
biome-agnostic engine for canals that carry water, ooze, slime, oil, tar or
fuel from a source into the terrain a colonist chooses.

Depth is the primitive. Every excavated cell carries two small integers — D,
how far below the surface it was dug (shallow, mid, deep, SUPERDEEP), and F,
how much liquid is in it — and everything else is a function of those two on
one cell: what it costs to cross, how much it holds, and which liquid surface
is drawn. We dig down; we never build up. There is no elevation model, no
height advantage, and no fluid simulation: liquid levels itself out on a
pulse, by sorting the deepest cells first and letting a full one overflow
into whatever has room.

A natural liquid body IS a source — deep terrain that is already full, which
is why it spills into a shallower channel dug at its edge. Liquid stays in
what has been excavated.

Shipped: the depth/fill grid and its pulse engine
(`RM_MapComponent_Excavation`), a dig designator that deepens a cell each
time it is used, depth-derived movement cost, a three-tier fill ladder on
vanilla's own edge-aware water ramps, and `FluidDef`s describing what a
source carries — water and tar for canals, plus the wider LiquidDef
registry (below) covering fifteen liquid types with their own terrain suites
and bottled forms. Bottles, buckets and barrels fill and wash at a
matching liquid's shore, and a buildable liquid tank holds a bulk stock of
one liquid at a time, filled and drained by the same containers.

A SUPERDEEP excavation is the trapping level and the only one: anything that
walks into one falls in and is held there whether the hole is dry or brimming,
and gets out only by climbing a ladder somebody built down there. Pull the
ladder and they stay. Depth touches shooting in exactly one way, and it is a
restriction rather than an advantage — whoever is in a superdeep hole can only
trade fire with whoever is standing right at its lip, both directions.

Burning liquids are built (a fuse creeps along tar or oil once vanilla fire
touches it) but not yet proven in a live game. Not yet built, and named so
nobody thinks they are missing: sluice gates and irrigation.

The engine writes the map's temporary terrain layer, which
is base-game machinery, and ships its own temporary terrains rather than
naming the Odyssey-only ones. Harmony is required.

MERGED IN 2026-09-16 (FLOWWORKS_BUILD_PROGRAM_1 Phase 1) — one mod now owns
the whole liquid domain, per the owner's ruling that depth is the single
primitive underneath all of it:

PITS. A pit is any canal cell dug down to superdeep — there is no pit
building. Whoever walks, is pushed or jumps in takes a fall and, if the pit is
as wide as they are, cannot climb out until a ladder stands in their cell.
They stay on the map, on the pit floor.

WATER EFFECTS (was mandrake.rm.manywaters). The generic water-effects
engine: animated river-steam ambience off a biome's own opt-in extension,
RM_DeepSand (impassable, fishable sand built the way vanilla deep water is),
and the coloured-water and coloured-slime terrain, fleck and bottle
families. Biome-agnostic; the Ash'karr wiring lives in RimUtinni.

LIQUID TYPES (was mandrake.rm.liquidtypes). The liquid registry: per-liquid
TerrainDef suites cloned off vanilla water — tar, ooze, propane, acid,
brine, coolant, ichor and the rest — plus the RM_LiquidProperties extension
the C# reads for what native fields cannot say (pH/corrosion, damage on
immersion versus contact).

RIVERS (was mandrake.rm.riverworks; merged 2026-10-05 — owner: "I think river
works needs to be part of flow works."). Rivers that move: moving river water
shoves pawns, corpses and loose items downstream. Chest-deep water is a fast
lane nobody wades out of, shallow water an edge lane you can still cross;
bigger rivers shove harder and a spring or torrential-rain flood makes every
river fiercer. Swept to the edge of the map and you are washed away — your
people walk home a few days later, and a letter tells you so. Ford stones laid
across shallow water cross safely, and colonists route to fords and bridges on
their own. The bank works: a weir built on the bank edge stops what the river
carries, calms a long stretch upstream and catches fish from the river's own
stock plus whatever this country's rivers bring down; a continuous line of bank
stakes holds back a spring flood like a levee, and any gap lets it in; let a
weir wear down and a flood breaches it, washing its catch downstream and
snapping the stake-line below it post by post. Silt-traps turn the bank soil
rich, and two ferry posts across a river string a rope nobody is swept off.
Every piece has a toggle in the Rivers section of FlowWorks' Mod Settings.

NOT merged, and staying siblings on the owner's boundary principle —
FlowWorks owns what a liquid IS and DOES; a machine that TRANSFORMS one
liquid into another is technology: GelatinousSlime (registers rows, keeps
its genes), WreckedMachines (distillation and every other conversion), and
FloodedCanyon (a flood-driver client).

name: RimMandrake: Explosive Knockback
author: mandrake
description:
Every blast throws everything light near it - people, animals, mechanoids, items and corpses - straight away from its centre. A mortar shell beside a person throws them three cells; lighter things fly farther, heavier things less, and anything too big (body size 2.5+) or too heavy (items and corpses over 75 kg) stays put.

Thrown pawns fly over sandbags and barricades, stop early against walls, closed doors and other pawns (taking impact damage for the distance they did not travel), and land stunned. Items on shelves stay on the shelf.

With FlowWorks: anything thrown into an open pit lands on the pit floor, and a person thrown in takes the fall and is held like anyone else who falls in. People already in a pit are never thrown out. (Blasts breaking pit covers is FlowWorks' own setting.)

With Gimme Some Slack: a colonist carrying a hose end drops it where they stood.

A thrown pawn cannot be thrown again until its landing stun ends plus a recovery window (120 ticks by default), so no blast can juggle someone. A shield belt that absorbs a blast absorbs the throw too, and pays extra charge for it: a strong throw can pop the belt.

Explosions only: Bomb (grenades, mortars, IEDs) throws; fire, EMP, smoke, firefoam and tox gas do not. Explosions from other mods throw only if patched with RimMandrake.ExplosiveKnockback.RM_KnockbackExtension (force; optionally maxThrowCells - its own maximum throw, impactFactor - scales impact damage, immuneBodySizeOverride - throws bigger bodies). The extension is read from the explosion's projectile ThingDef first, then its weapon ThingDef, then its DamageDef; the first one found supplies the whole configuration, or by the "unpatched explosions" setting (default 0%).

Every part has a Mod Settings toggle; all off is vanilla. Design: design/RimMandrake/explosive_knockback_design_2026-10-06.md.

name: RimMandrake: Kinetic Arms
author: mandrake
description:
A family of ancient kinetic-blast weapons whose shots throw people rather than wound them. Built on Explosive Knockback.

- Thudder grenade: a thrown concussion grenade that clears a doorway.
- Palm thumper: a sidearm that shoves one target straight away from the shooter.
- Slam launcher: a lobbed kinetic charge for the enemy's second rank.
- Repulsor rifle: every hit pushes the target back along the shot line.
- Kicker mine: a buried, rotatable plate that launches whoever steps on it in its facing, and re-arms with chemfuel.
- Thump shell: a wide, low-damage throwing shell for the ordinary mortar.
- Pulse cannon: a powered turret that stores pulse charges and shoves raiders away from your wall.
- Grav-ram: the strongest throw there is, up to 10 cells.

Each weapon sets its own maximum throw (grav-ram 10, thump cannon and thump shell 8, thudder grenade 6).

Also: the mechanoid thump cannon now throws farther than a mortar shell beside its impact.

Kinetic blasts do little or no wound damage and barely scratch walls. The palm thumper's shove never hurts on impact (an arrest tool); the grav-ram can move bodies up to size 3.5 (a centipede, never a thrumbo). With Gimme Some Slack, kinetic blasts sway overhead cords instead of cutting them. Shield belts absorb kinetic throws (Explosive Knockback). They kill only through what they throw you into: walls, pits, fire, other people.

These weapons are not crafted: they are found, mostly in ruins - an ancient-danger temple has a 35% chance (setting) to hold one kinetic weapon or a stack of thump shells. Pirates who looted those ruins rarely carry one on a raid (2% of armed pirates by default); no other faction does. Every weapon and the thump cannon change has a Mod Settings toggle; all off leaves the items inert in the world and the thump cannon vanilla. Design: design/RimMandrake/kinetic_blast_weapons_design_2026-10-06.md.

name: RimMandrake: Gimme Some Slack
author: Mandrake
description:
Drawn flexible pipes and wires to better display simple circuit-like plans underneath.

Cables: the conduit itself becomes invisible and keeps working exactly like vanilla conduit. A purely cosmetic layer reads the conduit network as a graph of the things it connects (generators, batteries, machines, junctions, the places where it disappears into a wall or rock and comes out again) and draws loose, too-long cords between connected neighbours over the walkable floor. Cords never cross a wall and never join two things that are not really connected. Breaks read at a glance: a conduit end still on a powered net sparks; a dead end lies limp. Nothing of theirs is saved, so adding or removing the mod mid-game is safe for them; the power overlay's connection lines are left alone.

Overhead lines: masts, lamp masts and wall brackets carry real power over open ground on sagging overhead wires that sway in the wind and may pass over roofed rooms. A cut or orphaned wire hangs from its insulator down to the break and sparks while live; explosions can cut a wire. A power-tap clamp quietly drains another faction's grid into yours without merging the two. Unlike the cords these are real buildings with saved links: removing the mod from a save that holds them loses them, with missing-definition errors.

Flexible hoses: thick, stiff hoses laid from a hose reel, flat when empty and plump while liquid flows, bound at both ends with dense cloth wraps.

Four looks, switched together in Mod Settings: Scrapper, Industrial, Modern and Futuristic. Everything lives in ONE Mod Settings entry with three tabs (Cables, Overhead lines, Flexible hoses); every behaviour has a switch, and each master switch brings the vanilla art back at once.

name: Jawa Plant Growth (local)
author: mandrake
description:
Planetary fast growth. One Harmony postfix on Verse.Plant.GrowthRate multiplies the composite growth rate of every plant from every mod, so nothing has to be enumerated and any plant a mod adds later is caught automatically.

Four bands, biome-aware (exactly one applies per plant):
- wild plants and crops x4.0
- trees x2.5 (wood stays a decision)
- plants on a terminator / poison-forest biome x0.4 (the one place on this world where growth has stalled)
- plants in the three wet biomes (Greentide, Miasma, Fever Wood) x10, trees x6.25 — the always-on groaning growth of the wet jungles (owner ruling 2026-09-21; replaces the x4 band there, does not stack on it)

The water-SOAK event multiplier (EXPLOSIVE_PLANT_GROWTH_1) is not here: it belongs to mandrake.rm.explosivegrowth and multiplies on top of whichever band applies.

Every number, the terminator biome roster and the exempt plant list live in Defs/JawaPlantGrowthSettings.xml and are read at startup, so tuning does not need a rebuild. The compiled defaults in RimMandrake.Utinni.PlantGrowth.PlantGrowthConfig are used only if that def is missing.

Exempt plants are untouched in every biome: the anima tree and the Gauranlen tree (their slowness is ritual and dryad pacing, not botany), ambrosia (deliberately scarce), and any plant whose growDays is already under 1 day.

The postfix scales the COMPOSITE GrowthRate rather than a single GrowthRateFactor_*, so environmental penalties (light, temperature, fertility, drought) still apply and the terminator case genuinely comes out slower than vanilla.

When mandrake.rm.explosivegrowth is active, this mod also loads ExplosiveGrowth/ (LoadFolders.xml): the campaign half of the explosive-growth plant roster and the RUT_BloomBurst incident (FLOOD_WITNESS_EVENT_1's map-scale bloom). Without it, those files are simply not loaded.

Load after Harmony. It is silent when it works: verify from the inspect string on a plant, which reads the boosted rate because it is computed from the same getter.

name: RimMandrake: Oracle
author: Mandrake
description:
The Oracle — in-game LLM wiring (design/RimMandrake/llm_ingame_wiring_spec.md), campaign-agnostic plumbing. In the campaign it is the NARRATOR's engine (the ship's old non-egoic mind voicing the nine gods); no god is the Oracle, and Ohm is only its first consumer. This build carries the transport plus ONE god-letter consumer (Ohm the All-Current, per design/RimMandrake/nine_voices_cast_bible.md), end to end, gated by two debug actions (Debug Actions Menu -> RimMandrake.Oracle) rather than any live game trigger yet:

"Selftest validator (no network call)" runs the register lint against canned good/bad text, launching nothing.
"Test Ohm letter (live call)" fires one real async call through OracleGameComponent and delivers a letter -- the model's text if it passes the register lint, the prescribed fallback if the call fails, times out, or the output is rejected. Nothing about this ships live to any consumer yet; the v1 posture (dormant vs consumer-live) is the owner's call after he sees this work.

Transport: the Claude Code CLI, run non-interactively as a child process -- `claude -p` with the persona block passed as --system-prompt and the context written to the child's stdin, reading its plain-text stdout. There is no HTTP call, no endpoint, no model string and no API key anywhere in this mod; the CLI authenticates through the machine's own claude.ai login (owner ruling 2026-09-05, CLAUDE.md "In-game LLM access is the Claude Code CLI, never a hosted API key").

ENVIRONMENT DEPENDENCY: this mod does nothing at all unless the Claude Code CLI is installed AND logged in on the machine running the game. That is a fact about the machine, not a Mod Settings value -- the only related setting is an optional full path to the claude executable, for when the game process's PATH does not carry it. With the CLI absent, logged out, or broken, every call fails and every consumer ships its prescribed fallback text: the game is whole with the LLM entirely absent, by design, and that is never allowed to become untrue.

No Harmony, no def patches. Everything is opt-in through Mod Settings behind a global kill switch (off = no process is ever launched) and a per-day call budget.

name: RimProperty
author: mandrake
description:
PROPERTY_FABRIC_BUILD_1 — the campaign-blind ownership/theft/perception fabric ruled at the 2026-08-31 brainstorming sitting (design/Jawa/ownership_settlement_spec.md, canon.yml ownership_fabric). A decaying-claim engine: claims are a set of (claimant, strength, basis, timestamp) records per Thing, virtual and computed by default (territorial/situational — zero storage, zero tick cost), recorded only for the exception list (stolen, purchased, claim-fee-paid, gifted, inherited, looted). Decay is lazy — evaluated on read, never ticked — at a rate set by a per-Thing recognizability score (quality, market value, a persistent Name, mechanoid identity). TakingEvent is the event spine every future verb emits into: act → claim resolution → authorization check → witness/perception roll → faction-record propagation (also lazy) → an unauthorized-taking hook other content binds a social-fight reaction to. Colony-side friction: each colonist is their own claimant, a per-faction Commons claimant holds unassigned faction property (the player colony's "Clan commons" is just the player faction's instance of this), and guests are ordinary Pawn claimants with a different Faction — the same mechanism, fully symmetric.

Carries NO Star Wars content, no settlement/district data, and no RimUtinni tuning (decay-curve constants here are generic engine defaults, not authored per-species/per-faction values) — see design/Jawa/ownership_settlement_spec.md's "Module boundaries" table. The pay-claim-fee and theft-haul verbs live here (absorbed SalvageClaim + TheftHauler, 2026-09-08). Other consumers ship separately: SETTLEMENT_VISIT_LOOP_1 (Inhabited), DISTRICT_TEMPLATE_LIBRARY_1, SETTLEMENT_VERBS_WAVE_1, and RimUtinni tuning data.

No Harmony hooks auto-fire TakingEvents from vanilla actions — that wiring is verb-job territory (SETTLEMENT_VERBS_WAVE_1). This mod is the API future code calls, proven with a plain GameComponent ledger, at the colony, with zero visit machinery.

Absorbed mandrake.rm.property (SETTLEMENT_VERBS_WAVE_1's salvage-law pay-claim-fee float menu order) into this mod.
Absorbed mandrake.rm.property (BUILDING_THEFT_HAULER_1's theft-haul uninstall heist verb, MayRequire-gated Muckraker Crab Droid patch included) into this mod.
RIMPROPERTY_ANIMAL_THEFT_1 (2026-09-08): more MayRequire-gated Droidworks loader chassis marked with TheftHaulerExtension (Imperial Labor Droid, KM1-series Mining Droid, KM1-B Excavation Droid, GE3-series labor droid); the RM_Steal TrainableDef, letting an Intermediate-or-better-trainability pet be trained to sneak off with a small unattended item; and a wild-animal instinct doing the same, gated by a WildTheftExtension mark on Core's own Raccoon. All three routes fire the same TakingEvent spine as every other taking here.

name: RimDefDump (local tooling)
author: Mandrake
description:
Local research tooling, not gameplay content.

Dumps the RimWorld def database to JSON at game load, AFTER all mods have loaded
and all PatchOperations have applied. This is the post-resolution ground truth
that an offline Defs/ scan cannot see: patch results, mod-vs-mod override
winners, true shortHashes, and resolved stat values.

Adds no defs, no Harmony patches, and no gameplay behaviour. It only reads the
def database and writes files.

INERT BY DEFAULT. It does nothing at all unless a request marker file exists at:
  %USERPROFILE%\AppData\LocalLow\Ludeon Studios\RimWorld by Ludeon Studios\DefDump\dump_request.txt

Marker contents select the scope:
  (empty) or "animals"  - animals.json + manifest.json  (fast, seconds)
  "all"                 - the above plus defs/<DefType>.json for every def
                          type with a database (slow, large)

Companion to Utils/animal_inventory.py, which is the offline authoring view.
This is the live verification view.

name: RimMandrake: Utinni — Rust Cathedral Roaches
author: mandrake
description:
RUST_CATHEDRAL_MECHANICS_1 §6 (the roaches — the land
cleaners), owner addendum 2026-09-07, verbatim: "reskin the cockroaches mod
to pertain to the Scarlands around the Rust Cathedral and the Rust Cathedral
itself. Both organic and artificial versions. Make them much smaller and the
synthetic ones strangely tough and powerful. Cleaners of the area on land
like the eels that live in the coolant rivers."

Donor: LingLuo.Cockroach (workshop 3196253802, "Rim cockroach"), already
active in the mod list. MEASURED independently this pass (dnfile metadata
enumeration of Ling_Cockroach.dll plus a direct read of the donor's own
1.6/Defs/Normal.xml and Patches/Core.xml — not copied from the kit spec
blind): exactly 5 TypeDefs in the whole assembly (ThinkNode_EatWastepack,
JobDriver_EatWastepack, Toils_FenXi, Hediff_DeadBombToQiaoKeli,
Verb_JumpToFace), no HarmonyLib reference, no game-wide hook — every class
binds only where a def references it. The donor's one patch
(Patches/Core.xml) does exactly one PatchOperationAdd, donor-scoped
(ResurrectMediumMech's ingredient filter), irrelevant here. An XML-clone
reskin is therefore safe and this mod is exactly that: CLONE, never
patch-in-place. The donor mod itself is untouched and stays active for its
own two creatures; nothing below references any of its classes, comps or
recipes.

Two new races, both bodySize-shrunk from the donor's 2 down to "small
scuttling thing" scale — deliberately, per stat, never by a flat "scale all
attributes" (bodySize does not scale melee damage or armor):

  - RUT_ScarRoach (organic, AnimalThingBase, bodySize 0.25) — roams the
    Scarlands' scar-dust in loose colonies (wildBiomes: RUT_Scarlands).
    Light armor (0.2/0.15), modest bite (4), high Wildness (0.9), no taming
    hook this pass.
  - RUT_CathedralRoach (synthetic, BaseMechanoidWalker, bodySize 0.22, own
    BodyDef RUT_RoachHex rather than the donor's Scorcher_SixLeg so this def
    never depends on the donor mod's presence) — donor-comparable armor
    (0.75/0.75) at a healthScale (1.6) that reads "strangely tough and
    powerful" for its size, exactly as the owner asked. Wild fauna, not a
    player-craftable mech: no RecipeDef, no turret verb, no death-bomb
    hediff. Wild-spawn wiring for mechanoid presence is a SEPARATE axis in
    this campaign (the_rust_cathedral.json roster's own "confidence" entry:
    mechanoid/Sentinel presence is "EXCLUDED BY DESIGN... never encoded in
    wild rosters") — this def carries no <wildBiomes> entry; it rides
    whatever already spawns the roster's other mech-vermin (GR_Mecharat).
    ❓ UNVERIFIED without a live quicktest, which this pass did not run.

Both are "cleaners, not vermin" — the land counterpart to the coolant eels —
via RM_EatCleanableExtension / RM_ThinkNode_EatCleanable
(mandrake.rm.creaturebehaviors, this item's one new C# class): a generic,
data-driven "forage a named item and/or filth, then consume it" mechanism
that generalizes the donor's measured ThinkNode_EatWastepack in the two ways
the task specified — no player-faction gate (fires for wild pawns too, via
the shared engine's Animal_PreMain insertTag) and filth is a first-class
target alongside named items (Wastepack), not just wastepacks.

NOT wired to any hum-mood/attitude system (owner ruling, 2026-09-07: "leave
the roaches out of the hum mechanics for now") — RM_MapComponent_BiomeAttitude
does not exist yet regardless (a different, unbuilt section of this item),
and nothing here references it. No freeze/scatter tell.

Salability — DECIDED (kit spec §6): both roaches join the salable list. The
organic butchers normally (useMeatFrom Megaspider, like the donor). The
synthetic's butcherProducts include RM_CathedralRoachShell (mandrake.rm.biomes, Rust Cathedral;
this mod's RUT_ twin was folded into it 2026-10-09), a small tradeable resource, alongside
steel. Neither is "watched" by any hum/goodwill mechanic — no comp here
counts or reports a harvest; this is deliberate (rationale: leaving the
roaches out of hum inputs as well as hum displays), reversible on the
owner's word like the ruling it follows.

Deferred, NOT built this pass (all noted, none silently dropped): a
taming/pet register, a synthetic-roach death sting, and bespoke art — every
texPath below is a placeholder (magenta/missing in-game until the art pipe
runs); do not read a texPath's presence as art having shipped.

Roster wiring: design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/rosters/the_rust_cathedral.json
and the_scarlands.json fauna arrays updated to point at these new defNames
in place of the donor's Ling_Cockroach entry, which the roster had placed in
the Cathedral itself (an earlier reading, predating this addendum's
organic/synthetic biome split).

name: RimMandrake: Gravship Landing Reveal
author: Mandrake
description:
GRAVSHIP_LANDING_FOG_REVEAL_1 (owner, 2026-09-12): you cannot pick a landing spot you cannot see.

When a gravship arrives at a tile with no map, vanilla generates the map, reserves a landing area near the centre and fogs everything except the flood-fill from that one spot. If the spot lands inside a walled complex (ruins, a junkyard, an injected structure) the landing picker shows a single room and the rest of the map is black — so the player lands blind.

This mod runs after vanilla's GravshipMarker gen step on gravship-arrival maps and unfogs every OUTDOOR region (unroofed cells), exactly what vanilla's own edge-unfog does on maps with no start spot. Roofed interiors — mountains, sealed rooms, dungeons — stay fogged.

Mod Settings: one toggle, "Reveal the outdoors before choosing a landing spot" (default on). Off = vanilla behaviour.

name: RimMandrake: Huge Things
author: mandrake
description:
Huge plants and huge animals that behave like their size. Mass has consequences.

The engine gives every plant and every pawn one cell, however big it is drawn. A
mushroom twenty cells across can only be clicked on the cell it grows from,
pawns walk straight through its stem, and walls get built inside it. A beast
the size of a house walks through a doorway, hides behind a sandbag and gets
penned like a chicken.

Huge Things fixes that for anything that opts in:

- A huge PLANT gets a solid trunk. The cells where its art touches the ground
  are solid (measured per species, and grown into as the plant grows), so pawns
  walk around it and nothing can be built inside it. You still walk under its
  cap. Clicking anywhere on its picture selects it. Trunks give partial cover,
  and shots into them hurt the plant.
- A huge ANIMAL gets a selection hitbox the size of its drawn body.
- A TITAN (any creature of body size 4 or more, or one a mod opts in) gets a
  size tier. Heavy, colossal and titanic creatures crush crates and plants,
  breach walls, hole thin roofs and leave rubble as they walk, struggle under
  overhead mountain, butcher for a curved yield, and the largest leave a corpse
  that becomes a harvest site worked over days.
- The biggest titans smash through giant plants, damaging them as they push
  past; smaller titans go around the trunks like walls.

With Large Pawns (neku.largepawns) loaded, titans also occupy 2x2 to 4x4
cells, using this mod's tiers; without it they stay one cell and everything
else still works.

Mod Settings: one master switch for giant plants and one for giant animals,
each with every detailed behaviour and its tuning beneath. All off is vanilla.

This is the engine only. A plant opts in with the RM_HugePlantExtension, a
race with the RM_HugePawnExtension or RM_TitanicExtension modExtension (or
simply a large enough body size). This mod replaces "RimMandrake: Titanic
Creatures" (mandrake.rm.titaniccreatures), which is now part of it.

name: RimMandrake: SW — Bestiary
author: mandrake
description:
Absorbed creature content: defs and art lifted out of mods that are being retired, so retiring them costs the campaign nothing.

MLIE_FAUNA_ABSORPTION_1 — absorbs content from `mlie.starwarsanimalcollection` (Star Wars Animal Collection) under an `RSW_` prefix, staged in waves. All 589 SoundDefs absorbed (per-creature Angry/Wounded/Death/Call vocal sets across 143+ creatures, plus ability sounds). Wave A creature geometry (Bantha ThingDef/PawnKindDef, wool/milk/leather/meat/horn items, blue-milk thought) is absorbed; Sarlacc was found not to be a creature at all (an Odyssey-DLC building system) and is out of this item's scope. Waves B/C (remaining species) are still open.

JURASSIC_RETIREMENT_ABSORPTION (2026-09-05) — eight creatures out of Jurassic Rimworld - Dinosaurs Only (Continued), `Mlie.JurassicRimworldDinosaursOnly`, retired by the owner that day. The eight are the five live creatures that survive design/Jawa/worldbuilding/creature_recognizability_rule.md as STRANGE (Baseopsis, Diplocaulus, Platyhystrix, Protosolpuga, Protovermes) plus the three CUT ones that review/recognizability/RESTORE_CANDIDATES.md argued should come back (Segnosaurus — the owner's own type-case for a dinosaur that reads alien — Holcorobeus and Termitotron). Each is an `RSW_`-prefixed ThingDef/PawnKindDef pair with its egg items, its art extracted from the donor AssetBundle, and every donor-only dependency (the AnimalDinoThingBase abstract, Leather_SmallDino/MediumDino, DinoChitin's butchering comp, the Carnotaurus SoundDefs) replaced with a vanilla equivalent. Per-file headers say exactly what changed.

BEASTS_OF_THE_RIM_RETIREMENT (2026-09-05) — `RSW_Jerba`, new content rather than a port. Beasts of the Rim (`mlie.beastsoftherim`) was retired the same day; it shipped a speculative-biology `Jerbal` that was never a Star Wars jerba. This is the real one: the shaggy horned Tatooine pack-and-milk beast, desert-banded for Ash'karr, reusing the already-absorbed unwooled bantha sprite at a third of the size in a pale dun palette. Iconic Star Wars creature, so the recognizability rule's icon carve-out applies.

Content plus two absorbed assemblies (Livestock light-aversion, Ikee thought-worker); BeastNorm patches target the mlie.starwarsanimalcollection donor while it remains installed.

MECHANICAL_FAUNA_MERGE_WAVE_A — five sibling mods absorbed in, folders retired:
Absorbed SeaBeasts (`mandrake.rsw.swbestiary`, SW_SEA_MONSTERS_ART_1) — 18 Naboo/Star Wars sea creatures (opee/colo/sando/scalefish/swarm families) with full art; its dev-only art review material (`art/`) was left behind in the emptied SeaBeasts folder, not merged.
Absorbed Livestock (`mandrake.rsw.swbestiary`, FORSAKEN_CRAGS_PREDATORS_BUILD_1 / LIVESTOCK_STARTER_TRIO_1) — Cindermare, Skarnix and karrask defs, textures and the Abyss_WildSpawns patch; its C# (`CompLightAversion`, Assemblies/RimMandrakeLivestockRSW.dll) was left in place, unmerged — Cindermare/Skarnix now depend on an assembly that ships outside this mod.
Absorbed HelixTellurox (`mandrake.rsw.swbestiary`, HELIX_TELLUROX_BUILD_1) — the Tellurox draft/pack beast def and texture; not yet wired into any biome's wild-spawn cast.
Absorbed JawaIkee (`mandrake.rsw.swbestiary`) — the Ikee-watching thought def; its C# (`ThoughtWorker_IkeeNearby`, Assemblies/JawaIkee.dll) was left in place, unmerged — the thought now depends on an assembly that ships outside this mod.
Absorbed BeastNorm (`mandrake.rsw.swbestiary`) — Law 3 of the beast normalization pass, a PatchOperationConditional set keyed to Star Wars Animal Collection defNames; this mod now also depends on `mlie.starwarsanimalcollection` for that patch to have a target. Absorbed SeasWaterline (mandrake.rsw.seaswaterline): Lane 1 of the seas program — Lake/Ocean wildAnimals for the 14-creature waterline cast.

SAND_SWIMMERS_MOD_1 (2026-09-09) — the sand-swimmer fish family for RM_DeepSand (its two items, RM_DuneCrawler and RM_GlassPearl, moved to mandrake.rm.stillsand under STILLSAND_BEDAZZLE_CONTENT_1) (ManyWaters), never fish-shaped: `RM_DuneCrawler` (the catch, a stackable Fish-category item), `RSW_SandStalker` (the predator that hunts it, ThingDefs_Races), and `RM_GlassPearl` (the rare prize, ThingDefs_Items) plus `RSW_RareSandCatches` (ThingSetMakerDefs) which also lands the stalker's corpse as a rarer catch. Art on all three is placeholder (reused vanilla icons/sprites, clearly flagged in each file) — owed. Ash'karr biome wiring lives in RimUtinni: UtinniPatches.

CAVERNS_PARITY_BUILD_1 ruling 5 (2026-09-18) — `RSW_Maguana`, the fireproof magma-patterned iguana, ported out of `biomesteam.biomescaverns` ahead of that mod's retirement so the creature survives the cut. ThingDef/PawnKindDef pair, its two egg defs, the donor's `BMT_Caverns_EggFertExtreme` abstract (kept, not flattened — its only delta from vanilla `EggFertBase` is the 999 °C max-safe temperature the egg needs), and `RSW_Leather_Magma` out of Biomes! Core. Stats, tools, damage multipliers, lifeStages and art are verbatim; the PathfindingFramework `PF_Movement_Magmatic` modExtension is dropped, same rule as the rest of the BiomesTeamPort absorption. Not wired into any biome cast by this mod.

LIVESTOCK_STARTER_TRIO_1 (2026-09-09) — `RSW_Onnik`, the kiln-belly: a feed-cycle industrial animal with a real generated body sprite (conformed from the owner's picked mockup) and a new `CompKilnBelly`/`CompKilnFeed` pair (Assemblies/RimMandrakeLivestockRSW.dll, alongside karrask's own CompLightAversion) — feed it three spaced doses of `RSW_KilnClay` in a day for a glazed `RSW_FiredCeramicware` batch, or dump it all at once for worthless `RSW_CrackedCeramicShards`. Zero new job types. Karrask's own statBases/Mass was found double-scaled by bodySize (StatPart_BodySize multiplies whatever the def states) and corrected to the vanilla flat-60 convention. The trio's third creature, moornak, is still unbuilt — its spec conflicts with a later, richer owner ruling in the design doc and needs that call made before anyone writes its def.

AA_JOE_DESERT_PORT_BATCH_1 (2026-09-20) — `RSW_GreatDevourer` (retired 2026-10-08: now the franchise-free `RM_Gulloth` in LongShade), `RSW_Groundrunner` and `RSW_MatureFleshbeast`, ported from Alpha Animals (`sarg.alphaanimals`, an active mod dependency, so their art and cross-references stay live-donor rather than copied) for RUT_Desert at the owner's ruled 0.5 weight. Every donor-C#-only comp/render-tree/thinkTree/thingClass (VEF.AnimalBehaviours, AlphaBehavioursAndEvents) is dropped per the BMT_FAUNA_ABSORPTION_1 precedent; the creatures keep their stats, bodies and art. `JOE_Cephalope` was NOT re-ported here — it turned out to already be absorbed verbatim by STAT_NORM_WAVE2_RETIRE_1 (2026-09-11, `UtinniPatches/Defs/Absorbed_Cephaloids/`), donor mod already retired that day; only its RUT_Desert/RUT_ExtremeDesert biome wiring was still owed and is now landed there.

author: mandrake
description:
SHIP_VERMIN_MOD_1 — owner ruling, 2026-09-11, verbatim: "gather
all the 'ship infesting' critters together into a single mod 'ShipVermin' that
allows the mechanics, creatures, and future cool ideas to emerge. Some are
cute, some are hideous, some live inside, some can live outside in vaccuum
(the mynock for example)." One home for every ship-infesting critter, so a
future species lands here instead of spawning its own mod.

SHIPVERMIN_FREE_TIER_BEASTS_1 — owner ruling (card, typed, 2026-10-07): "Make
the free tier have its own beasts that get patched by the Star Wars bestiary
when active. Same mechanics same mod otherwise." This mod depends on no
franchise content. It ships its own cast:
  - RM_Skivvik: a vacuum-proof hull leech that drifts to a powered hull,
    breeds (soft cap 3 / hard cap 12 per map, group tag "ShipVermin") and
    gnaws lights, conduits and laid floor.
  - RM_Rattagh: a sociable, toxin-proof pest rodent of wreck voids.
  - RM_Gorrud: a nocturnal predatory rodent of holds and wrecks.
  - RM_Fethrik: a fuel mite that sprays chemfuel in a cone (RM_FethrikFuelSpew).
When mandrake.rsw.swbestiary is loaded, that mod's own patch
(Patches/ShipVermin/RSW_ShipVermin_CanonCast.xml) gives its canon creatures the
same mechanics and swaps them into the same four nest slots
(RM_ShipVerminCanonSwapExtension). Mechanics are unchanged either way.

The breeding/seek/gnaw machinery is mandrake.rm.biomes' CreatureBehaviors kit;
this mod sets it on RM_Skivvik in Defs/ThingDefs_Races/RM_ShipVermin_Cast.xml.
RM_Alert_ShipVermin is the population alert (group tag "ShipVermin").

WRECKAGE_VERMIN_SPAWN_1 (2026-09-12), owner ruling verbatim: "Yes vermin
should be able to spawn from wreckage." RM_CompProperties_VerminNest /
RM_CompVerminNest is a generic "nest under the wreckage" comp: attach it via a
comps-list patch to any wreckage ThingDef and it periodically spawns one wild
pawn from the settings-enabled nest roster nearby, gated by the same
RM_MapComponent_VerminPopulation group-tag pool the breeder respects (default
tag "ShipVermin", hard cap 12), so a nest and a breeding population press
against ONE shared ceiling. This mod does NOT decide which ThingDef counts as
wreckage — a campaign's own patch layer wires the comp onto its own defs
(Utinni layer: Patches/WreckVerminNest_ShipChunk.xml in mandrake.rut.patches).

Mod Settings: alert on/off, fuel spew on/off, wreck-nest on/off, a nest rate
multiplier, and one checkbox per nest slot (labelled with whichever creature
fills the slot).

Art: the four free species render with tinted vanilla placeholder textures
(sparrow, rat, boomrat, megascarab). Their own art is owed.

name: RimMandrake: Explosive Plant Growth
author: mandrake
description:
EXPLOSIVE_PLANT_GROWTH_1. Water-soaked plants grow where you can watch them — and every soaked plant is a countdown.

RM tier: nothing here knows what campaign or planet uses it.

THE SOAK. Ground becomes SOAKED when qualifying fresh water arrives in quantity, and dries back over hours to a day. Routes: a flood pushed in by another mod (RimMandrake: Flooded Canyon), irrigation (a dug FlowWorks channel holding fresh water soaks the ground beside it — rivers and lakes never do), a salt-line surge's fresh side (Environmental Hazards' gradient axis), and any weather a roster names as soaking. Soaked plants grow x10 ON TOP of whatever ambient rate the rest of your mod list gives them. Salt, fungus, and plants whose slowness is a mechanic (anima, gauranlen, ambrosia) never soak.

THE CHARGE. A soaked plant that reaches full size keeps going: it swells past natural size, and it tells you, in a fixed order — the ground darkens and sprouts, it swells, its hue shifts wrong, it trembles, it creaks, and then it goes silent. Then the top.

THE TOP belongs to the PLANT, never the ground it stands on:
  - Churn (the default): it splits, dies, drops its produce and sows a ring of sprouts that keep going. It respects your floors and walls.
  - Burst (dry-adapted plants only): a pop, chaff, bruises and knockdown nearby (never lethal on its own), premium produce scattered — and a sown ring that ignores your zones, floors and doorways.
  - Tinder: a burst whose debris is fuel.
  - Slime: the ring turns the ground to slime.
  - Rupture (contaminated plants): a gas cloud, spawned things, sprouts, and mutations for anyone in the cloud without a full vacuum seal.
  - Flush (giant trees): it swells inside and survives, silently.

PLAYER VERBS. Harvest a swollen plant for extra produce. Cut it to defuse it — though once it trembles, the last swing is a gamble. Keep ground dry. Grazing animals (and a dry-air blower, where another mod ships one) suppress encroachment for a few days.

Every mechanic has a Mod Settings toggle; defaults are the shipped behaviour. Plant tops are data: an RM_ExplosiveGrowthRosterDef (by name, silently skipping absent plants) or an RM_ExplosiveGrowthExtension on a plant you own. Soak/suppress are exposed as RimMandrake.ExplosiveGrowth.ExplosiveGrowthAPI for other mods to call by reflection.

Ships the IncidentWorker behind a map-scale bloom (RM_IncidentWorker_BloomBurst); a campaign layer names the IncidentDef and the bloom plant.

The performance gate (TPS on a jungle-density map under a full-map soak) is OWED to a live session; no density is promised until it runs.

name: RimMandrake: Lore Stages
author: Mandrake
description:
STAGED_LORE_BUILD_1 — descriptions that change as a story is learned.

A def's description, settle warning or label is rewritten to match how far a campaign's reveal ladder has advanced, so a place can read as an inexplicable wasteland until the player earns the truth and then read as what it is. The engine only; no lore text lives here.

HOW: every display surface that matters reads a def FIELD at draw time (the world tile inspector reads BiomeDef.description directly, Thing.DescriptionFlavor is a virtual with no backing store, the settle confirmation re-reads BiomeDef.settleWarning every time), so a field write shows on the next frame and no Harmony patch is needed. Ludeon ships the same idea in the base game: Building_VoidMonolith stages its description by campaign level.

THE TWO TRAPS IT HANDLES: (1) ThingDef.descriptionDetailedCached and HediffDef.descriptionCached are private memoized fields that NO engine path ever clears, so trade/transfer rows, storage filters and hediff tooltips would keep serving the previous stage's text for the rest of the session — this mod nulls both by reflection on every apply. (2) Defs are process-global and are not reloaded between savegames, so a stage-5 colony's text would still be on the def when a stage-0 save loads — every apply resets to the shipped baseline first and then applies the current stage from scratch.

WHAT SHIPS: GameComponent_LoreStage (scribes a per-ladder stage into the .rws, applies on FinalizeInit — which covers both a new game and every load) and RM_LoreStageTableDef, the data-side ladder table that content mods provide. Ladders advance independently. Dev-mode debug actions under "Lore stages" set any ladder's rung and dump what every staged field currently holds.

Loads and does nothing at all when no RM_LoreStageTableDef is present.

name: RimMandrake: Oasis Maker
author: mandrake
description:
OASIS_MAKER_BUILD_1 (owner ruling, 2026-09-24, verbatim: "machines that
create oases slowly when placed near shaded terrain near rocks. Placement is
key. We should guide it with green red area selections... Makes obtaining the
ancient machines a treasure type."). Spec: design/RimMandrake/oasis_maker_machines_spec.md.

A treasure-class ancient building (`RM_OasisMaker`, minifiable) that, once
placed on cold shaded stone, wakes after a short attuning window and then
grows an oasis around itself ring by ring, on its own clock — no power, no
fuel, no colonist labor. Terrain climbs a stepwise natural ladder
(Sand/SoftSand -> Gravel -> Soil -> SoilRich at the margin; Soil -> Mud ->
Marsh -> WaterShallow at the innermost ring, forming a real, fishable,
stockable pool at the machine's heart) — never floors, never constructed
terrain, never existing water, never stone. Placement is guided by a live
green/red projected-footprint overlay that recomputes per ghost move, the
same shape as vanilla's `PlaceWorker_WatermillGenerator`: red means the
hard floor (shaded cells + standing rock nearby) is not met and the machine
refuses to place; green shows the oasis the current spot would actually
grow, sized and paced by how good the spot is. Interrupting it (uninstall,
destruction, losing its shade/rock) freezes growth forever — everything
already converted stays; nothing this mod does ever reverses a cell.

**Acquisition (RULED, owner typed, 2026-09-24): "They are sold but very
expensive. Same tech as moisture farming itself. You can start a colony with
some of those. And priced accordingly."** Not craftable in v1 — the machine
is tagged for exotic-goods trader stock (`ExoticMisc`, treasure-class market
value) and is an ordinary minifiable buildable, so it is legal starting gear
in the scenario editor exactly like any other tradeable minified building.
Quest obtain/sabotage hooks are deferred to the quest-design passes per the
spec; this mod ships the mechanism only.

Tier: RimMandrake (`RM_`) — works on any map with shade and rock, not tied
to any one biome. Feature-gated: Mod Settings carries a master on/off plus
every rate and floor number named in the spec (shade/rock floor, attuning
length, base ring time, per-ring growth factor, radius cap band).

**Pool integration**: a newly grown `WaterShallow` cell fires the public
`RimMandrake.OasisMaker.RM_OasisPoolIntegration.PoolCellCreated` event
(map, cell, source="RM_OasisMaker") so a grown oasis registers with the
Stocked Pool kit's bookkeeping (`STOCKED_POOL_BUILD_1`,
`RM_MapComponent_PoolStock`) exactly like a natural pool once that kit
subscribes — see this mod's own rimflow item for the exact contract, since
that component did not exist yet when this mod was built.

**Art**: the spec's own build-size table lists the comb-silhouette sprite
pass as its own S-sized line item separate from this mechanism sitting
(alongside the deferred quest weaves) — this build ships with a placeholder
texture pending that pass, tracked in the same item.

author: mandrake
description:
Mirrors that move sunlight. SOLAR_MIRRORS_MOD_DESIGN_1 (design/RimMandrake/solar_mirrors_mod_design_2026-10-04.md).

A mirror throws a patch of sun onto a cell you pick. In that patch the shade is gone: it is hot, animals that hide from the sun route around it, and plants get more light where the sky is dim. Light reflects best back toward the sun's side and worst straight away from it. Walls, rock, closed doors and roofs stop a beam. A mirror standing in shadow throws nothing, unless another mirror lights it, so mirrors can be chained.

Buildings:
  - Signal mirror (1x1, no research). Aimed by a colonist (a re-aim job).
  - Static mirror (2x2, any metal; silver and gold reflect best). Aimed by a colonist. It does not track the sun, so where the sun moves its patch of light slowly sweeps.
  - Heliostat (3x3, powered). Aimed instantly and holds its target as the sun moves. Without power it freezes where it is and becomes a static mirror.
  - Sun-stone (1x1). Reads lit or unlit.
  - Solar furnace. Smelts with no fuel and no power, but only while concentrated light (two or more mirrors) falls on it. Indoors it warms its room.
  - Glazed aperture. A glass wall that mirror light passes through, on under the roof into the room behind it: a mirror-lit, mirror-warmed greenhouse.
  - Heliograph. By day a colonist at a sunlit signal mirror can flash a friendly settlement within reach and open talks with it.

Defence: hostile people standing in a beam slowly go glare-blind and shoot worse, unless goggles or a gene protect them.
Heat: where several beams overlap the light is stronger than the sun, and it feels hotter there, never past the biome's limit.
Upkeep: sand, grit and ash storms dull mirrors in the open until a colonist cleans them.

Ancient mirror fields: on the Long Shade, where the sun never moves, a map can hold a field of seized ancient heliostats before a sealed vault. Free their bearings, turn each between its old brass pins, and light every sun-stone to open the vault. Every field is checked to be solvable before it is placed.

Every effect has its own switch in Mod Settings (with an "all off" button that leaves inert decorative buildings). Mirror light is our own grid on top of the shade grid; it never adds a new kind of heat.
