name: RimMandrake: Warcasket
author: mandrake
description:
WARCASKET_SUIT_CLASS_1. A cross-cutting heavy survival-apparel class, generalized:
it names no biome, faction or campaign and is playable standalone on any generated RimWorld
planet. Owner ruling, 2026-09-28 (WASTELAND_BEDAZZLE_SITTING_1), verbatim: "Warcaskets REDEFINED
cross-cutting: very resistant to extreme temps + vacuum + toxins, an alternative to space suits
and ocean access, but very slow, bulky, prone to failure under compound threats — a primitive
tank around a person."

RM tier: nothing here knows what campaign or planet uses it. The Wasteland biome (and the frozen
Utinni campaign's own Wasteland instance) is this suit's primary use case — Junkers wear a
further-adjusted variant to extract fuel from ruined ground — but the suit class itself works
anywhere extreme temperature, vacuum or toxic-terrain protection matters: any DLC's space
exposure, any biome's toxic fallout, any modded ocean/brine shore.

Ships, all togglable in Mod Settings (defaults = shipped behavior, MOD_OPTIONS_RETROFIT_1
doctrine):

  1. RM_Warcasket — the base suit. Real stat coverage for all three hazard classes (extreme-temp
     Insulation_Cold/Insulation_Heat, vacuum via Odyssey's own VacuumResistance, toxin via
     Biotech's own ToxicEnvironmentResistance), a heavy MoveSpeed/WorkSpeedGlobal penalty ("very
     slow, bulky"), and a real compound-failure mechanic: RM_CompWarcasketIntegrity tracks how
     many hazard classes are simultaneously active against the wearer and rolls a genuine failure
     chance once two or more stack, damaging the suit and injuring the wearer with a tendable
     RM_WarcasketBreach hediff — not flavor text, an actual risk that scales with how compound the
     threat gets and how damaged the suit already is.
  2. RM_WarcasketJunker — a Junker-adjusted variant, and warcasket sarcophagi (wastes.md §7: "a
     dead Junker in an adjusted warcasket is a sealed salvage-within-salvage: suit, tools, and the
     half-extracted core still in its grips"). The suit seals onto its wearer at death, so ordinary
     stripping leaves it on the body; a colonist cracks it open from the corpse's right-click menu
     to recover the suit, the welded tooling and RM_HalfExtractedCore, a reactor core that doses
     everyone near it until it is locked in a cask bay.
  3. Terrain-survival wiring: RM_HazardousTerrainProtection (a summed apparel stat, same shape as
     TheRot's RM_SheenProtection) and RM_MapComponent_HazardousTerrainImmersion, a general
     hazard engine (not warcasket-specific — any apparel granting the stat helps, on any map) that
     applies RM_TerrainImmersionHazard to a pawn standing on deep/non-walkable water terrain
     without enough protection. Scoped deliberately to non-walkable ("must swim") water only —
     an ordinary shallow ford or marsh margin every biome already has pawns cross freely is never
     the hazard; only water nothing can simply walk across is. 🔴 This is TERRAIN survival only:
     it grants no dive verb, no MapPortal access, no sea-floor teleport of any kind. A sea FLOOR
     stays reachable only through a gravship's own RM_SeaDiveHatch — "the ship is the only way
     down and the only way back" (owner ruling, 2026-09-26). A warcasket lets its wearer stand
     safely at the edge or wade the shallows and margins of a hostile sea or brine pool; it never
     lets them dive to, or return from, the floor beneath one.

  4. RM_CaskBay — the lead-lined cask bay the sitting approved (BENCH slate item 7, owner "yrs"):
     "a shielded hardpoint that lets the ship haul the Throat's casks". A cask-only storage building
     that needs gravship substructure, so it flies with the ship; while shielding is on, stored
     toxic wastepacks never dissolve and stored cores give off no dose.

name: RimMandrake: Watchers
author: mandrake
description:
WATCHER_CREATURES_MOD_1: shy creatures that sit, peek out, watch you, and jerk back under
cover when anything that is not their own kind comes near. A standalone kit (owner ruling
2026-09-30); a biome's roster draws on it. Design: design/RimMandrake/watcher_creatures_kit_design_2026-10-02.md.

Ships:
  1. The kit. RM_WatcherExtension on a race opts it in; the comp is injected at startup, so a
     member writes XML only. Hidden -> peeks out -> watches (turns to face the nearest pawn) ->
     flinches and hides when a non-own-kind pawn comes within its flinch radius, a neighbour's
     alarm reaches it, one of its own cues holds, or (optional geophone) something large swims
     under the sand nearby -> re-emerges after a delay. A hidden watcher always leaves a sign on
     its cell: no animal vanishes without a readable sign.
  2. Medium lock: a watcher wanders only on its medium terrain and walks back to it when found
     off it; it only ever hides on its medium.
  3. Death (owner ruling 2026-10-08): watchers cannot be flushed. Nothing can aim at a hidden one,
     and a visible one is an ordinary target. Almost no damage kills one, and fire, explosions and
     acid reach it even while it hides. It leaves small, sad remains of dubious value.
  4. Alarm ripple: when one ducks from something close, or dies, a few neighbours duck too, in a
     short wave that cannot loop.
  5. First member: the piinnok of the Stillsand, the watching glass, locked to deep sand.
  6. Mod Settings: master, hide and flinch, turn to face, stay on medium, geophone, alarm ripple,
     one toggle per cue, flinch radius, re-emerge delay, max active watchers per map.

Works alone. With RimMandrake: FlowWorks the piinnok's medium (deep sand) exists; with
RimMandrake: Baroque Biomes it filter-feeds the sand and its lenses sink
for submerged sand swimmers.

name: Geonosian Brain Worms
author: Mandrake
description:
BRAINWORM_MOD_BUILD_1, built to design/RimStarWars/brain_worm_spec.md.

A Geonosian hive parasite. The worm itself is near harmless in the open; it is
only dangerous as a payload. It burrows into a LIVING host and rides a staged
infection -- latent, influenced, puppeted -- until the hive is driving the body.
Cold kills it: below freezing the parasite dies and is expelled, so on a tidally
locked world the cure is a PLACE. Surgery is the risky fast path.

Three infection vectors, all ruled by the owner 2026-09-11:
  1. Geonosian ruin dungeons  -- egg clusters in ancient-complex room loot.
  2. Salvaged cargo           -- the RSW_BrainWormCargoPod incident.
  3. Weaponized-egg war retribution -- craftable mortar shells that burst into
     worms where they land. Carry a mortar to their map, shell them, leave.

RULING, PERMANENT (owner 2026-09-11, verbatim: "Never corpse-walker. Too gross."):
this mod NEVER animates a corpse. Every puppeting path requires a living pawn --
CompRSWWormBurrow refuses a dead target, the puppeteer comp stops the moment the
host dies, and the worm race sets canBecomeShambler false so Anomaly cannot make
one out of it either. Do not add a dead-host path to this mod.

No Harmony: the puppet think tree rides vanilla's own Humanlike_PostMentalState
insertTag hook, so there is no patch to collide with.

Private campaign mod, not for redistribution.

ART OWED: every texPath in this mod currently points at a vanilla stand-in
(megascarab body, high-explosive shell). Nothing renders magenta, but nothing
here is drawn yet either.

name: Bandolier North Fix — Star Wars KotOR Resources and Materials
author: Mandrake
description:
Adds the missing north-facing worn art for two of the four bandoliers in Star Wars KotOR Resources and Materials: bandolier_chewbacca and bandolier_traveler.

WHAT THE PLAYER SEES WITHOUT IT — worse than a missing bandolier

The bandolier does not vanish when a pawn turns its back. RimWorld's Graphic_Multi, finding no north texture, fills the slot from the south at 180 degrees, so the pawn gets its CHEST POUCHES DRAWN ON ITS BACK — and the def's own drawData puts the north view at layer 65, on top of everything else the pawn is wearing. Wrong art rather than absent art, which is why it reads as intentional and nobody reports it.

No log line is possible. "Failed to find any textures at" fires only when EVERY direction of a set is missing, and these sets have east and south.

Both items carry wide generation tags — chewbacca on KotORAccessory_any / heavy / outlaw / trooper / bandolier, traveler adding civilian and richcivilian — so they land on colonists, traders and raiders alike, and north is roughly one facing in four. This is the most-seen missing-facing defect we have found in this mod set.

CONTENTS — 20 files

  SWApparel/Accessories/bandolier_chewbacca/Apparel_{Male,Female,Thin,Fat,Hulk}_north
  SWApparel/Accessories/bandolier_chewbacca/Apparel_{Male,Female,Thin,Fat,Hulk}_northm
  SWApparel/Accessories/bandolier_traveler/Apparel_{Male,Female,Thin,Fat,Hulk}_north
  SWApparel/Accessories/bandolier_traveler/Apparel_{Male,Female,Thin,Fat,Hulk}_northm

      All 512x512, the canvas of every other file in both sets. Ten art files and
      ten tint masks. A complete set here is 32 files and each of these two ships
      22, missing north and northm for all five body types.

      THE DONOR'S ORIGINALS: there are none. Neither north nor northm exists at
      any load folder for either set. The other two bandoliers in the same folder
      — bandolier_double and bandolier_knife — ship north for all five body types
      and are healthy.

HOW THE ART WAS DERIVED — from the author's own finished work, not invented

Nothing here is a fresh drawing. The two complete sets in the same folder are the
specification, and they were measured rather than eyeballed:

  1. NORTH IS A MIRROR. bandolier_knife's north agrees with its own MIRRORED
     south 77.4% by silhouette, and with its unmirrored south only 34.3%. A strap
     worn over one shoulder swaps sides when you walk round the pawn.
     bandolier_double is an X-cross and scores 96% either way, so it neither
     confirms nor denies — the knife decides it.

  2. THE BACK OF A BANDOLIER IS BARE LEATHER. Both of the author's north views
     are the strap with its front furniture gone: his bandolier_double north is
     the X-cross without the pouch blocks his south carries, and his
     bandolier_knife north is the strap and belt without the three sheathed
     knives. Pouches hang on the chest.

  3. HIS MASK SAYS WHICH PIXELS ARE FURNITURE, so that step is not guesswork.
     CutoutComplex tints mask-RED by the apparel's stuff colour and leaves
     mask-BLACK fixed, and in both target sets the mask-black regions are exactly
     the ammo cells and the buckle while the mask-red is the leather and the hip
     pouch. The author drew the split himself; we read it.

  4. THE LEATHER COLOUR IS HIS TOO. It is sampled from the strap pixels his own
     mask calls red — the gaps between his ammo cells, which is the only place
     the bare leather of THIS bandolier is visible anywhere in the set — then
     quantised into five stops and laid across the band, darkest at the edge and
     lightest at the core, which is how he shades every strap in the folder.

  5. THE MASKS ARE A SOLID RED FIELD, because after step 4 there is no
     fixed-colour furniture left on this facing for a mask to protect. That
     matches the author: his own Apparel_*_northm.png files are a solid red
     field, shipped at 16x16. Ours are the same field at the art's own 512x512,
     where the file cannot be mistaken for a truncated one.

  The generator is shipped in Source/build_north.py, with the two survey scripts
  that produced the measurements above (Source/survey_donor_north.py,
  Source/survey_broken_sets.py) and the test that rejected the first recipe
  (Source/test_mask_recipe.py).

WHY IT IS A REPAINT AND NOT AN INPAINT — the attempt that was thrown away

The obvious build is "delete the mask-black furniture, then grow the neighbouring
pixels back over the holes". It was written, run, and rejected on sight. On
bandolier_chewbacca the ammo cells cover 42% of the strap, so what grows back
into the holes is not leather but the shadow gaps BETWEEN cells, and the result
reads as a chewed, mottled band. There is no clean strap surface anywhere in the
set to inpaint from — which is exactly why the leather has to be sampled and
relaid rather than recovered.

That failure was caught by testing the recipe against bandolier_knife, where the
author's real north exists to score against. It reproduced his north 77.2% where
mirroring alone scores 77.1%: no gain. The test is shipped as
Source/test_mask_recipe.py so the next person does not repeat it.

WHAT THE BUILD REFUSES TO SHIP

The generator gates every file before writing and prints what it rejected:
canvas must equal the donor's; the alpha channel must be pixel-for-pixel
unchanged, because a repaint that moves the silhouette is not a repaint; at least
one fully opaque pixel must exist; and at least 10% of the drawn area must
actually have changed, or the furniture is still on the pawn's back and the file
is a mirror pretending to be a fix.

  The faint alpha fringe these files carry (1.09% on the Hulk traveler) is the
  DONOR'S, present at the identical figure in his own south, and inherited rather
  than introduced — the repaint never touches the alpha channel at all.

WHERE THE DEFS ARE

  1.6/Defs/ThingDefs_WeaponsArmorsGadgets/Apparel_SWAccessories.xml
    chewbacca  lines 383-387 and 403-432
    traveler   lines 478-482 and 497-525
      line 426  wornGraphicPath      SWApparel/Accessories/bandolier_chewbacca/Apparel
      line 427  useWornGraphicMask   true
      line 428  drawData/dataNorth/layer  65

The Graphic_Single on line 385 governs the ground and inventory item art only.
The worn graphic comes from wornGraphicPath and is always resolved as
Graphic_Multi over path_BodyType_facing. There is no visibleFacing, no
bodyTypeGraphicPaths and no per-facing suppression anywhere in either def, so
nothing declares north deliberately absent.

LOAD ORDER MATTERS HERE, AND THIS ONE DOES NOT SIT WITH THE OTHERS

Star Wars KotOR Resources and Materials ships its textures LOOSE — Textures/ at
the mod root, no AssetBundles folder and no .bundle anywhere in the mod. Between
two loose files at the same path RimWorld resolves by load order, so this mod
must load AFTER the donor.

That is a real constraint rather than a formality: the donor sits LATER in the
load order than the slot our other art-fix mods occupy. Placed with them, this
mod would be overwritten by the donor and would be completely invisible, with no
error and no log line. It must go after Star Wars KotOR Resources and Materials,
not beside mandrake.missingartfixes.

Swept the whole workshop tree and the local Mods folder: exactly one mod ships
these texture paths, so nothing else is supplying a north and nothing else is
being overridden.

name: MSE Droid North Fix — Outer Rim: Droid Depot
author: Mandrake
description:
Adds the missing north-facing art of the MSE-6 repair droid in Outer Rim - Droid Depot.

The droid's PawnKindDef declares Graphic_Multi, which means RimWorld expects four directions, but the mod only ever shipped two: south and east. When a direction is absent Graphic_Multi silently falls back to the south texture, so an MSE droid walking AWAY from you turns around and shows you its FRONT. Nothing is logged — "Failed to find any textures at" fires only when every direction of a set is missing, and this set has two.

No defs are patched, no code runs, and Outer Rim - Droid Depot is not altered. This mod drops one loose PNG at the path the donor's own def already asks for.

CONTENTS

  OuterRim/Droid/MSE_north
      The back of the MSE-6 repair droid. 256x256, 1,051 bytes, 8.86% of the
      canvas inked.

      THE DONOR'S ORIGINAL: there is none. Droid Depot ships MSE_south
      (256x256, 2,707 bytes) and MSE_east (256x256, 2,064 bytes) and no north
      texture at any load folder. The absence was confirmed against the 1.6
      AssetBundle rather than against the mod's stale loose folder: the bundle
      manifest lists DroidDepot/Textures/OuterRim/Droid/MSE_east and
      DroidDepot/Textures/OuterRim/Droid/MSE_south and no MSE_north entry, so
      there is nothing to override and nothing to conflict with.

      HOW OURS WAS BUILT AND VERIFIED: the silhouette and the black keyline are
      copied PIXEL-FOR-PIXEL from the donor's own MSE_south, so registration,
      canvas, bounding box (97, 80, 159, 178) and 3 px keyline weight are exact
      by construction and cannot drift. Only the interior is re-authored — the
      front bevel is replaced by a plain rear panel with a horizontal vent seam
      and two vertical panel joints, using the donor's own measured greys
      (upper plate 231, lower panel 178, vent seam 96, panel joints 148), which
      is what the back of a box droid should read as. The generator is shipped
      in Source/draw_mse_north.py.

WHERE THE DEF IS

Outer Rim - Droid Depot's own PawnKindDef asks for a four-way graphic:

  1.6/Defs/ThingDefs_Automatons/Animal/Droid_MSEDroid.xml
    line 81  defName        OuterRim_MSEDroid
    line 89  texPath        OuterRim/Droid/MSE
    line 90  graphicClass   Graphic_Multi
    line 113 recipeIcon     OuterRim/Droid/MSE_south

NO LOAD ORDER REQUIREMENT — AND THAT IS DELIBERATE

This mod deliberately declares no loadAfter, because it does not need one.

On 1.6 Outer Rim - Droid Depot serves its art from an AssetBundle, not from
loose files. Its LoadFolders.xml swaps the v1.4/v1.5 "Common_Old" folder for
"Common" under v1.6, and Common/ holds nothing but
AssetBundles/neronix17_outerrim_droiddepot. The loose droid PNGs still sitting
in Common_Old are not loaded on this game version.

RimWorld resolves a texture as loose file in any active mod FIRST, then base
game resources, then AssetBundles — so a loose PNG beats a bundled asset
regardless of which mod loads first. In this particular case the point is
academic twice over, since the bundle contains no north texture to be beaten.

If Outer Rim - Droid Depot ever ships its own MSE_north, this mod would still
win by being loose, so unsubscribe it at that point.

name: Sarlacc — Native Habitat (local)
author: mandrake
description:
SARLACC_HABITAT_BUILD_1 — the sarlacc's native-habitat build, off
`design/Jawa/worldbuilding/sarlacc_native_habitat_draft.md` (ACCEPTED whole,
all forks RULED, 2026-09-12 owner sitting, §8).

THREE STAGES, ONE CREATURE:
- Stage I — the swimmer (RSW_SarlaccSwimmer): a mobile sub-sand predator, modeled
  on Anomaly's Devourer per the owner's explicit direction (§8) — sub-sand
  approach, swallow-whole via the vanilla CompDevourer, its "digestion" re-themed
  in every message as the press wringing a drink, not eating. Cut-free
  counterplay retained (nothing new added that bypasses normal combat).
- Stage II — the anchored (RSW_SarlaccAnchored): what a swimmer becomes when it
  roots. Fork 1: swimmers ROOT IN PLAY — a swimmer that runs out of its birth-water
  reserve, or finds a buried seep (RSW_DeepDesertSeep marker), anchors visibly on
  the map and stops being a pawn. It strikes rarely, at its own mouth, at whatever
  stands beside it (the doc's "tithe").
- Stage III — the cistern (RSW_SarlaccCistern) and its drained end-state, the
  throat (RSW_SarlaccThroat): a landmark-scale reservoir. Fork 5: the breach is
  the ONLY kill — no hit-point bar, no poison route, the deed is done in person
  by interacting with the reservoir wall. Breaching it runs the doc's §4.4
  consequence order (flood messages, ecosystem-death messages, conversion to the
  drained throat) at v1 fidelity — see the item file for what is simplified here
  versus the full pocket-map dungeon interior, which is owed to `sarlacc_spec.md`'s
  separate (also not-yet-built) KCSG ladder and explicitly out of this doc's own
  stated scope (draft §0: "Does not touch... the KCSG/pocket-map build ladder").

SEVEN CHANGED-RETURN HEDIFFS (Fork 8, all seven ship): the wrung, salt-eyed, the
stillness, the tithe, the bloom, pressed, taken-and-returned (draft §4.5). A pawn
that survives being swallowed and regurgitated by a swimmer or an anchored mouth
is granted one, occasionally two, picked by this build (dealt by context is owed
once the pocket-map interior exists to distinguish "taken in the press" from
"taken on the shore" — see item file).

TRIBAL STAGE LABELS (Fork 9): the tribes' own words for the four stages are
DRAFT flavor text in this build — Seeker / Debtor / Collector / Paid, echoing the
Sun-Debt's own theology ("the sun lends and the sand collects... we take back what
was drawn") — and ship as description flavor only, pending the owner's yes per
the ruling's own wording. The doc register (swimmer/anchored/cistern/throat)
remains the defName/mechanism vocabulary regardless of the owner's call on the
flavor names.

OWED, NOT IN THIS BUILD (see infrastructure/state/items/SARLACC_HABITAT_BUILD_1.md):
world tile 2920 relocation off the Weeping Stones oasis; placing 2-4 cisterns in
true deep desert; the full pocket-map dungeon interior (press/gallery/reservoir
levels); DBH thirst-need integration for the breach flood (Fork 6: DBH thirst is
confirmed live so this is a real wiring task, not a design question); real sprite
art (every texPath here is a placeholder reuse of existing Anomaly/vanilla art,
never magenta, always a real file); a RimUtinni-side patch making
taken-and-returned sacred/unclean specifically to the Sun-Debt ideoligion (this
mod only ships the generic RSW-tier hediff, per the naming-tier doctrine that
faction-specific reactions are RimUtinni content, not RimStarWars).

THE SWIMMER'S ROAD (LONGSHADE_BEDAZZLE_MECHANICS_1): once per map, ever, on a Long
Shade map, one swimmer comes up at the edge and swims shade to shade toward the
biggest dew ring, leaping at flesh on the dew line, and roots there for good. Every
take leaves disturbed sand and a message. Uses mandrake.rm.creaturebehaviors'
shade-patch graph when that mod is active (loadAfter, soft).

Requires the Anomaly DLC (Devourer's body/render-tree/comp are reused by
reference) — every def here that touches it is MayRequire-gated.

name: RimMandrake: SW — Trophy Craft
author: mandrake
description:
WYYYSCHOKK_FANG_PENDANT_1 (owner's direct spec, 2026-09-13,
verbatim): "add this awesome concept to the game for the Wildsteam/Blackstar/
Deep Tribe factions, as they all have a concept of respected hunting:
Wyyyschokk fangs on a tribal pendant showing the bravery of the person. These
should have social consequences for being worn by implying the person is
quite brave (with those factions), and be a trade good elsewhere on planet
regardless."

Ships the mechanism, owns no campaign data:

  1. `RSW_WyyyschokkFang` (ThingDef, ResourceBase) — a stackable trophy
     resource, small marketValue on its own. A patch
     (`RSW_TrophyCraft_WyyyschokkFangDrop.xml`) attaches it as a
     butcherProducts entry on the third-party `Wyyyschokk` ThingDef
     (`mlie.starwarsanimalcollection`, Star Wars Animal Collection —
     confirmed by the same species-ownership search `RimMandrake: SW —
     Shokk`'s About.xml already recorded: there is no RUT_/RSW_-owned
     Wyyyschokk def anywhere in this repo, only PatchOperations against the
     donor's). A patch that matches nothing logs nothing, so this mod loads
     fine with or without that donor installed — it simply never drops fangs
     without it.
  2. `RSW_Apparel_FangPendant` (ThingDef, apparel) — crafted at a hand tailor
     bench from fangs + cloth (the "textile cord"), low work, no research
     prerequisite (tribal tech level). Worn on a brand-new
     `RSW_Neck` ApparelLayerDef, bodyPartGroup `Neck` only:
     🔴 **VERIFIED, not guessed** — the live def dump (232 ThingDefs
     covering `Neck`, captured against the ~630-mod list) shows 153 of them
     share the vanilla `Middle` layer while covering `Neck` (shirts, vests,
     robes), so a Neck-only accessory on `Middle` would silently block
     wearing a robe, a vest or most tribal wraps at the same time — exactly
     the silent collision this item's own doctrine warns about. Reusing a
     third-party layer (`Jewelry`'s or `Romance On The Rim`'s `Accessories`)
     would trade that collision for a soft dependency on a mod that can be
     removed out from under it. Owning a brand-new layer used by nothing
     else is the only zero-collision, zero-dependency answer, so that is
     what ships: the pendant can always be worn with anything else in the
     630-mod list.
  3. `RSW_TrophyCraft_ObserverBraveFang` (ThoughtDef, social, worker
     `RSW_ThoughtWorker_ObserverFactionApparel`) — a plain, Harmony-free
     `ThoughtWorker` (spec option (a); the ideoligion precept route is
     explicitly rejected — precept budget is FactionDef-fixed, so a named
     precept would be design register, not mechanism). It reads its target
     apparel defName and its list of "regards this as brave" faction
     defNames from a `RSW_FactionApparelThoughtExtension` `DefModExtension`
     on the ThoughtDef. **This mod ships that extension EMPTY** — RimStarWars
     tier does not know the Utinni campaign's factions. `RimUtinni Patches`
     (`mandrake.rut.patches`) wires in the real three via
     `WyyyschokkFangPendantFactions.xml`, keeping campaign data in the RUT
     tier where it belongs. +opinion magnitude is a Mod Settings slider,
     default ON.
  4. Trade: `RSW_Apparel_FangPendant` carries `tradeTags: ExoticMisc` (the
     same tag `Jewelry_Necklace` uses to sell everywhere) and a real
     `MarketValue`, so any settlement or trader buys it — no faction check
     gates the sale. The Bazaar's worldTag weighting could later make
     hunting-tribe settlements pay MORE for it; that seam is noted, nothing
     Bazaar-side is built here.

**Live quicktest owed** beyond this build's offline `validate_patch.py` pass:
butcher a Wyyyschokk, craft the pendant, spawn a Wildsteam/Pirate/TribeCivil
observer and an unlisted one, confirm the opinion delta appears only for the
listed factions, confirm the pendant sells to a vanilla trader. See
`infrastructure/state/items/WYYYSCHOKK_FANG_PENDANT_1.md`.

Entries cover the Utinni campaign's own content and the free RimMandrake and RimStarWars mods the scenario runs. An entry whose subject is not loaded in your game is shown as absent from this world, never as a task left undone.

name: RimUtinni: The Reckoning
author: Mandrake
description:
WEBWORK_EGG_RECKONING_QUEST_1. The assassination quest family split out of
WEBWORK_EGG_BLACKMARKET_BUILD_1, per that item's own close report: "needs a new C# plant-watcher
verb, several unresolved numbers, and live-game verify outside its offline scope." Design:
design/Jawa/worldbuilding/biomes/webwork_egg_blackmarket_2026-09-24.md §2 (the quest family) and
§3 (the hatch mechanism), S5 rulings 2/3/6/7.

Ships one QuestScriptDef family, "The Reckoning": a debtor's outpost with three solution paths —
(1) pay the Cartel directly (a TradeRequest silver delivery, same machinery
RUT_WildsteamEggBounty already uses), (2) defeat the outpost in the open (vanilla
site.AllEnemiesDefeated), (3) plant an RM_OllathrixEgg inside the outpost undetected and let it
hatch that night (the one genuinely new C# verb this family needed).

RULINGS IMPLEMENTED, verbatim from S5:
  2. Hatch mechanism: STAGED QUEST EVENT. RM_OllathrixEgg carries no CompHatcher and never
     hatches anywhere outside this quest — RM_QuestPart_EggHatch spawns the one RM_Ollathrix
     PawnKindDef directly once planted and the map reaches its next night window (23:00-02:00,
     the design's own literal citation). No second egg def, no comp on the shared item.
  3. What hatches: JUVENILE. The spawned spider is the SAME RM_Ollathrix kind at a fixed
     biological age within its own lifeStageAges' AnimalJuvenile band (0.2-0.4 x 14y
     lifeExpectancy = 2.8-5.6y; 4.0y picked, INVENTED midpoint, disclosed) — no new PawnKindDef,
     per §0 ruling 2's one-race-one-kind law. It is spawned via the same
     PawnGenerator.GeneratePawn + MentalStateDefOf.ManhunterPermanent pattern
     IncidentWorker_AggressiveAnimals and Scripts_ItemPodThreat.xml's own manhunter-pack reward
     threat already use — a real, losable hostile animal, not a scripted kill.
  6. Total deniability CONFIRMED. An undiscovered egg-hatch kill (QuestNode_End on EggHatched)
     carries no goodwillChangeAmount at all — the target's faction never learns anything.
     Discovery before the hatch (EggFoundBeforeHatch) is the ONLY branch that costs goodwill,
     and only then.
  7. Quest-only planting stands. RM_OllathrixEgg is never given a hatch mechanism outside this
     quest's own RM_QuestPart_EggHatch — a player cannot buy eggs and free-plant them as weapons.
     The free-form colony-weapon version is WEBWORK_EGG_WEAPON_VERSION_1, explicitly out of
     scope here.

MECHANISM GAPS DISCLOSED (checked live against the decompiled engine via RimSage — nothing here
is guessed): the design's own §2a hand-waves path 2 as "vanilla shuttle/caravan-delivery
machinery" and names a bedroom-specific marked cell for the plant — neither exists as a nameable
vanilla mechanism. No vanilla QuestNode captures "deliver a captured pawn to a settlement," and
no SitePartDef places a single trackable, capturable NAMED individual the way DownedRefugee/
ItemStash's own site parts do for THEIR pawns. So: the "target" is a flavor-only QuestNode_
GeneratePawn (Villager, faction=$siteFaction) used for grammar and for goodwillChangeFactionOf,
never placed on the map; the outpost's whole garrison (SitePartDef Outpost, requiresFaction,
minThreatPoints 300 — genuinely "standard machinery" per the design's own words) stands in for
"his men," and path 2's success is the real vanilla site.AllEnemiesDefeated signal (an actual
fight, a real win condition) rather than a scripted capture. The egg-plant check is "any
RM_OllathrixEgg lying roofed and unfogged anywhere on the site map" rather than a single marked
bedroom cell, since no vanilla API identifies which building is "the target's bedroom" inside a
procedurally generated Outpost. Both are disclosed simplifications, not silent inventions.

INVENTED NUMBERS (same disclosure posture as RUT_WildsteamEggBounty's own header — picked
within or near the design's own ❓ ranges, not silently guessed, all in
RUT_Reckoning.xml's own header comment):
  - expireDaysRange (offer window) 4~8, matching this campaign's own quest family convention.
  - Completion timer 10-15 days (design's own ❓ range, used as given).
  - Path 1 payoff: ~2x the base reward (design's own "roughly 2x").
  - Path 2 goodwill penalty -8 (open, visible abduction — legal-adjacent per §2a).
  - Path 3 post-plant discovery goodwill penalty -25 (the design doc's own ❓-25, carried
    forward as given rather than re-invented).
  - Post-plant per-hour discovery chance 3%.
  - Juvenile hatch fixed biological age 4.0 years.
  - minRefireDays 30 and rootSelectionWeight 0.15 on the natural-pool fallback route.
  - rootMinPoints 300, matching Outpost's own minThreatPoints exactly (not arbitrary).

FIRING ROUTES (skill §7): RUT_Reckoning_CartelOffer is the primary route (givenBy Traders,
randomlySelectable false — vanilla's givenBy tag is generic to ALL traders, not filterable to
one TraderKindDef, so "the Cartel hands you the contract" is fiction over a generic-trader-offer
mechanism, disclosed). RUT_Reckoning_Rumor is the low-weight natural-pool fallback for colonies
that never meet a trader, ParentName-inheriting the same root tree (skill §3: ParentName
inherits the whole tree and text packs).

OFFLINE-ONLY VERIFY: validate_quest.py clean, dotnet build clean against the real installed
Assembly-CSharp.dll. NOT verified: whether GenHostility.AnyHostileActiveThreatToPlayer's
"undetected" reading matches what a human would call stealthy, whether the Outpost SitePartDef
reliably generates a roofed indoor cell the egg can be dropped in, and whether the juvenile
spawn is tuned right in a real fight — all three need a live dev-mode "Generate quest" pass,
which is bridge/game-up work this item's own scope note excludes (needs: offline).

Depends on mandrake.rm.webwork (RM_OllathrixEgg, RM_Ollathrix) and mandrake.rut.patches
(RUT_Jawa_HuttCartel, the FactionDef the settlement-finder node is scoped to).

    (mynocks cling to hull ribs, scavrats and womp rats nest in cargo, zhakkas
    feed at tanks), then it keeps producing slowly under Ship Vermin's shared
    cap of 12 per map. Strip it to end it.
  - The specimen (Band C): very rarely, one escape pod lands holding a single
    white lab rat — the one Earth animal on the belt, by the owner's ruling.

Where: only on Fall Line maps by default — a map whose tile carries the
RUT_FallLine tile mutator, or whose world feature is named one of the Fall
Line region names. A Mod Setting lets the events fire on any map instead.

  - Fall survivors (Band B): factionless feral droids (Droidworks' utility
    kinds) that run from people, hide in wreckage and fight only when
    cornered. One drifts in off the flats now and then; some fallen wrecks
    hide one that bolts when a colonist comes within 25 cells. Capture it and
    a wild-keyed data spike wipes it clean.
  - Feral people (Band B, §8b feral races): crash survivors gone feral
    ride the same routes and behaviour. Enslave or recruit one and they
    keep a permanent Fall Line scar; unlike a droid, nothing wipes it.

Not here yet (filed): placing
the RUT_FallLine mutator on the region's tiles of the frozen world, and the
two wreckage creatures that are not yet ported.

Every switch is in Mod Settings ("Fall Line Arrivals").

name: RimMandrake: Utinni — Propane Lake Mechanics
author: mandrake
description:
PROPANE_LAKE_PIPE_MECHANICS_1 — the propane lake's pipe/vent/saturation build ladder (design/Jawa/proposals/propane_gas_deep_design.md §9, RULED owner sitting 2026-09-01).

Four mechanisms, all riding new comps and one careful combat-path hook:

1. RUT_GasVent — self-igniting puffs, no depletion until a RUT_VentPump is built adjacent and actively pumping; removing the pump while the vent is still live triggers a violent map-wide flammable release that clears by wind (CompGasVent).

2. GasSaturationTracker (MapComponent_GasSaturationTracker) — a map-level saturation meter: transient during a release/rupture event, perpetual in hand-authored caverns and dead-sarlacc dungeons (with rotstink paired in). Exposes a deflagration-risk query used by a single, isolated postfix on ranged fire resolution (Patch_GasSaturationDeflagration) implementing the ruled 0-20/20-50/50-80/80+ curve — melee, thrown-without-a-charge and unpowered tools are untouched because they never call Verb_LaunchProjectile. Feature-gated in Mod Settings; off by default effect strength is tunable, never silent.

3. CompPipeNetwork/CompPipeRupture — pipe segments, a RUT_PipePump and a RUT_PipeValve join an adjacency network (MapComponent_PipeNetworks). A ruptured segment (fire damage, explosion, or the dev "trigger rupture" gizmo) spawns a standing jet that does not go out on its own — only closing a reachable valve on the SAME network depressurizes it. Left running past a tuned delay on a faction-owned map costs real goodwill with that faction.

4. RUT_VWake wiring (CompVWakeAgitation, patched onto the existing creature, no def rework) — the creature ships with plain manhunterOnDamageChance since COMMISSION_LEDGER_CLEANUP_1; this adds the ruled "agitated by pump noise" half: RUT_PropaneAgitation (a temporary hediff, speed/awareness up) applies while any RUT_PipePump within range is running, and clears when pumping stops.

5. RUT_SaturationHeistRaid (IncidentWorker_SaturationHeistRaid) — row 6, "saturation heist": once a map's own saturation has crossed the ruled 50% coin-flip band, an incoming raid re-equips every gunner it would otherwise have spawned with the ruled non-flammable/non-thermal/non-explosive loadout (vibroblade, vibro-double-blade, sonic pistol — MayRequire mandrake.rsw.armoury — falling back to vanilla neolithic melee so the swap is real with or without that mod) rather than sending riflemen to deflagrate themselves. Reuses vanilla's own faction/strategy/arrival pipeline in full; only the fire-gate and the post-spawn re-equip are new.

Not built here (explicitly out of scope for this pass, left for the item's own "work owed" if picked up again): the full pump-reach QuestScriptDef traversal template, and the tanker-run/tar-interplay rows the design doc itself cut.

description:

name: RimUtinni: Ship Shields — Modulated Plasma Fields
author: Mandrake
description:
SHIELD_MODS_LEVERAGE_1 — the bespoke building-scale shield comp,
ruled owner/2026-09-04 by card (design/Jawa/canon_reintegration_plan.md sec G.9:
"bespoke building-scale comp, NOW... the new C# system's maintenance cost
accepted"), superseding the earlier survey's lean toward forking a Vanilla
Expanded engine (VEF's CompShieldField turned out to be a pawn-apparel comp,
not building-scale; see the item file's source-verification section).

One `RUT_ShieldGenerator` building, one field active at a time, switched by
installing a module (shd:loadout-tradeoff) rather than four separate
buildings:

  - Bubble/kinetic (shd:bubble-not-wall, default, no module needed): a real
    subclass of vanilla's own `CompProjectileInterceptor` (the same base
    class Odyssey's native gravship shield generator uses,
    RimWorld/CompGravshipShieldGenerator.cs) rather than a fork of any mod's
    engine. Forcibly draining it to 0 hit points triggers a collapse
    explosion (shd:bubble-not-wall's "prone to overheating or even explosion
    when forcibly collapsed").
  - Thermal veil (shd:thermal-veil, module-gated): partially rejects outdoor
    temperature drift via `GenTemperature.ControlTemperatureTempChange`
    applied straight to `Room.Temperature` (the same primitive vanilla's own
    `Building_Heater`/`Building_Cooler` use), power-only, never a full
    cancellation — the room still climbs toward extremes, just far more
    slowly.
  - Cryo envelope (shd:cryo-envelope, module-gated): the mirror of the
    thermal veil, holding back severe outside cold via the same
    `ControlTemperatureTempChange` primitive at a stronger correction
    factor, plus its own distinct cost — a small constant interior-heat
    drain every interval, the honest reading of the ruling's "pulls in heat
    in both directions... slowly decreases the temperature within the
    ship." The ruled "glowing red-orange black body radiation" visual is not
    built (no existing vanilla VFX primitive found for it; real art/VFX for
    this whole mod remains owed).
  - Particulate screen (shd:particulate-screen, module-gated): clears
    weather-deposited filth in radius each interval, repels small wild
    animals out of radius (a real vanilla flee job), and negates the one
    concrete vanilla mechanism matching "vapor, bio contamination... damage
    completely" — airborne Toxic Fallout exposure for pawns and crops in
    radius. Vanilla has no other direct-HP-damage weather effect to negate
    (sandstorms/rain only touch accuracy, move speed and mood).

Canon-wide "slow-moving things pass through every shield" (shd:shield-
collapse-evacuate) is implemented as a Harmony prefix on
`CompProjectileInterceptor.CheckIntercept`, scoped to this mod's own
`CompShieldGenerator` only — vanilla's native gravship/mech shields are left
untouched pending a separate, larger call on whether to extend it further.

Predictive shield-failure alerts (shd:shield-collapse-evacuate's evacuation
warning): the bubble generator now watches its own hit-point decline and
sends one warning letter when collapse is projected within about an
in-game hour, clearing once it recovers.

Landing-hazard advisory (shd:no-hard-landing-gate): a Harmony postfix on the
confirmed-live `Scenario.PostGravshipLanded` hook sends a single non-blocking
letter if the landing map has an extreme-heat, airborne-particulate, or
severe-cold hazard with no matching shield configured and powered.

The design doc's other half of that same ruling row is now built too:
`ShieldHazardExposureTracker` (a per-map `MapComponent`) applies periodic
`Deterioration` damage to Things near the ship for every hazard that stays
active and unshielded, with the application rate (never the per-hit amount —
the ruling's own text is "full raw strength from tick one," not a ramp)
doubling after a long unshielded stretch, plus a second, harsher letter at
that point. Landing on active lava (the ruling's named worst case) fires one
immediate damage burst and letter, unconditional on shield state — no shield
configuration makes lava safe. Both pieces are Mod Settings toggles. See the
item file for the full account.

Full spec: design/Jawa/proposals/ship_shields_deep_design.md. Survey and
scoping history: infrastructure/state/items/SHIELD_MODS_LEVERAGE_1.md,
research/Jawa/shield_mods_survey_2026-09-02.md.

name: RimUtinni: The Unfinished Line
author: Mandrake
description:
Nobody on this planet mass-produces droids. The Geonosian Foundry Hive knows how, and the factory patterns sit latent in their databases, but they are left-behind workers from a factory site, not a whole people, and they cannot run the line. The Free Droid Enclaves need it badly: they are escaped droids who can only repair each other, and every one they lose is lost for good. The Jawa are the only ones who can stand between them.

A five-beat quest chain (design/Jawa/proposals/droid_mass_production_quest_chain_2026-10-02.md). The chain is offered once the Free Droid Enclaves like you (goodwill 20), you can repair droids at a shop, and day 30 has passed. Each beat follows the last after a few days; a failed beat is offered again, and too many failures break the chain.

Built: the chain itself and all five beats. 1, "The Count": three badly damaged Enclave droids brought to your shop (your own good parts or worn ones; the Enclaves judge the job by the worst droid that walks out). 2, "The Envoy": two Hive overseers and their Enclave escort stay four days; accepting starts a truce the Enclaves broker, and harming a guest ends the truce and the chain. 3, "The Pattern Cores": recover three cores from the old silicax foundry ruin, past its wild droids, and refuse (or accept) an Imperial broker's offer for them. 4, "The Tithe and the Hands": load an Enclave shuttle with a large material tithe and one skilled crafter, lent to the line for ten days. 5, "First Light": hold your colony against an Imperial strike through the line's first run. Where the line stands (the site choice) is not built yet, so the later beats happen at your colony.

Mod Settings ("The Unfinished Line"): chain on/off, the goodwill and day gates, days between beats, failures allowed per beat, the brokered truce on/off, and per-beat tuning (the ruin, the broker, the tithe scale and the crafter asked for, the first run). Dev mode: Debug actions, Quests, "Offer The Unfinished Line (skip gates)" and "offer next beat now".

name: Jawa Utinni Statues
author: Mandrake
description:
Statues of the Utinni faith (STATUE_ART_EXPANSION_1, design/RimMandrake/statue_mods_spec.md, Mod 1).

The sculptor's table can carve an Utinni votive (small), statue (person-sized) or grand statue (2x2).
Once one is placed, its "Dedicate" button chooses who it honours: any of the Nine (Ishko, Ohm, Oomo,
Mob'Unloo, Rekko, Ta'Baa, Zizzik, Sh'kaar, Ozzik), grand idols of Ohm, Rekko and Sh'kaar, the
sand-crawler relief, or the three votives (the Bandolier, the Droplet, the Tally). The carving, the
name and the "Honours" line follow the choice. Any colony can carve them.

idol (chemfuel; Sumpgas in the Utinni campaign) whose sun-disc crown carries a flame and lights the

name: RimUtinni: Wildsteam Egg Bounty
author: Mandrake
description:
WEBWORK_NEST_EGG_ECONOMY_1, S6 ruling 2 (owner, question card, 2026-09-24):
"the Wildsteam pay an egg BOUNTY — they pay to destroy eggs, the same shape as the mandible
bounty. A second, lower-paying legal outlet beside the smugglers' jackpot." Per the follow-up
2026-09-24 sitting (webwork_egg_blackmarket_2026-09-24.md §1e/§1f): the Wildsteam route pays
market value x0.5-0.7 as goodwill-plus-silver, deliberately below the black market's premium —
"virtue pays less."

Ships one QuestScriptDef (RUT_WildsteamEggBounty), built on the exact same vanilla
QuestNode_TradeRequest_Initiate/TradeRequestComp machinery Core's own TradeRequest quest and
this repo's own RUT_FungalSoilTradeRequest already use (see that quest's own header for the
pattern this one copies) — the Wildsteam "buy" the delivered eggs at a below-market price and
the fiction is that they destroy them; mechanically this is an ordinary settlement trade
request, the same as every other one in the campaign.

THE ONE DEPARTURE FROM THAT PATTERN: vanilla's own QuestNode_GetNearbySettlement has no
faction-filter field (the same open question RUT_FungalSoilTradeRequest.xml already flags for
its own Moisture Farmer case) — this quest is specifically the Wildsteam Clan's own bounty, not
a random nearby settlement's, so a small custom QuestNode
(RM_QuestNode_GetWildsteamSettlement.cs) finds the nearest live settlement belonging
specifically to RUT_Jawa_WildsteamClan via Find.FactionManager.FirstFactionOfDef (verified
live in this repo, src/RimUtinni/PyrelandsMechanics/Source/PyrelandsFactions.cs) and
Find.WorldObjects.SettlementBases, standard RimWorld.Planet API.

Depends on mandrake.rm.webwork (RM_OllathrixEgg, the requested item) and mandrake.rut.patches
(RUT_Jawa_WildsteamClan, the FactionDef this quest is scoped to).

NOT built here (WEBWORK_EGG_BLACKMARKET_BUILD_1's own scope, S5 rulings, a separate sitting):
the Cartel black-market trader/caravan kind, the Bazaar broker channel, the tradeability-All
patch, and The Reckoning assassination quest family. Those consume the same RM_OllathrixEgg
item this mod's quest also prices against, but neither item's build touches the other's files.
